evidence.readmeExcerpt: # doubao-image — generate images with the local Doubao app > 面向：使用者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20 Registers one tool, `generate_image`, that drives the **locally installed and logged-in Doubao (豆包) desktop app** to produce a picture, saves the full-resolution file, and sends it into the conversation. ``` plugins/doubao-image/ ├── package.json # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch, exports ├── cordis.patch.yml # bundle patch: the loader row ├── lib/ │ ├── index.js # cordis plugin: the generate_image tool │ ├── doubao.mjs # app launch, prompt submission, result harvest │ ├── cdp.mjs # dependency-free Chrome DevTools Protocol client │ ├── watermark.mjs # removes Doubao's own overlay, with a self-check │ ├── image.mjs # minimal PNG codec + raster helpers │ └── generate.mjs # CLI driver, for testing without spending a model turn └── test/ # node --test (no DSH, no app, no network) ``` ## Install ```bash # from npm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-doubao-image # or from the repository root — the leading ./ matters: DSH anchors relative specs # against your current directory, otherwise pnpm would resolve it inside the profile dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/doubao-image ``` Then restart DSH (or reload the profile). The tool appears as `generate_image`. ## Use ```bash # exercise the whole path without going through the model node plugins/doubao-image/lib/generate.mjs \ --prompt "一只戴黄铜护目镜的橘猫，坐在双翼飞机驾驶舱里" \ --style "黏土质感 C4D 渲染，暖色夕阳光" \ --out ~/Pictures/doubao ``` The tool takes `prompt` (required) plus `style`, `composition`, `aspect`, `negative`, `count`, `dir`, and `reuseCurrentChat`. ## How it works, and why it is built this way Doubao ships a **full Chromium** (`Contents/Helpers/Doubao Browser.app`), and its launcher forwards unknown flags, so starting it with `--remote-debugging-port` yields a real CDP endpoint. That is the whole reason this works without the macOS Accessibility permission that `osascript` would need — which matters, because that permission is not granted on this machine. The findings each step depends on, all established by probing the running app: | Step | What is actually true | | --- | --- | | Launch | Doubao holds a **singleton lock**. A normally-launched instance never opens the debug port, and launching again just forwards to it. The app must therefore be quit and restarted — the first call costs ~10–40 s. | | Attach | `doubao-chat` is the real 1200×800 window. `doubao-launcher` is a 400×600 **sidebar that also accepts prompts** and renders results at 90 px, and `doubao-chat` is *additionally* served as an empty `hello` shell. Identification uses live window size plus the presence of the editor, never the URL alone. | | Type | The box is `div.tiptap.ProseMirror[contenteditable=true]`. `execCommand('insertText')` goes through the same `beforeinput` path a keystroke does, so the app's own state and send button update. Assigning `innerText` would not. | | Detect | The status sentence 「已生成 N 张候选图」 is the completion signal, not the image count — the grid mounts placeholders before the renders arrive. | | Harvest | The picture in the grid is a `cpreview_wm1` render behind an overlay, and its full-size sibling `` is a bare `data:image/svg+xml` **placeholder with no pixels**, so the bytes cannot be read from the grid. Instead the tool clicks each thumbnail to open the image viewer and uses the app's own `[data-testid=edit_image_download_button]`, which writes the file to `~/Downloads`; the tool then moves it to `dir`. | `dsh-doctor`-style checks live in the unit tests: the output schema must stay in sync with `execute`, because a tool that returns a value without a declared schema is refused at registration and takes the **whole plugin tree — and every DSH boot, the desktop app included — down with it**. ## The watermark Doubao stamps 「豆包AI生成」 into the bottom-right of every saved picture. It is an overlay the app composites on, not part of the artwork, which is what makes removal a solved problem instead of an inpainting guess. All of this was measured, not assumed: | Property | Measurement | | --- | --- | | Position | Anchored to the bottom-right corner; a glyph mask from one image correlates with an unrelated image's corner at **NCC 0.949** (inverse control −0.949, exactly symmetric) | | Scale | Proportional to the image's **short side**, not its width: 2048²→321×69 box, 1365×2048→214×46 box, both giving width/short ≈ 0.1567. Verified on a second sample per shape | | Blend | Plain alpha composite `C = a·W + (1−a)·B`, fitted at **a = 0.638**, W = 234.4, RMS residual 6.3/255 | | Soft edge | Glyph interiors measure a = 0.63 while the antialiased rim ramps to 0 — which is why a hard 0/1 mask left a visible outline | Removal inverts the composite per pixel, and estimates the artwork behind the mark by coarse-grid interpolation that excludes masked pixels. The output PNG is encoded losslessly (round-trip delta verified 0). **Self-check.** The `verifyOnFlat` helper turns "does it look clean?" into a number: on a flat-background sample the artwork behind the mark is a constant, so any residual offset inside the glyph area *is* the watermark that survived. Measured on a flat 2048² sample: **residual 46.3 → 0.0 (100% removed)**. On a photograph the same metric would be meaningless, so it detects a non-flat frame (background IQR > 8) and says so instead of printing a flattering zero. **Scope.** This targets this one overlay, at this one anchor, with this one calibrated blend. It is not a general watermark remover. It exists for internal reference material — animation reference, storyboards, internal review. Doubao's official API (Volcengine Ark) returns images with no watermark at all, and that is the right channel for anything published or commercial. **Stripping is off by default** (owner's decision, 2026-09-25): an image comes back with Doubao's own 「豆包AI生成」 badge unless the caller explicitly asks for `stripWatermark: true`. Keeping the badge is the safe default — it is what makes a picture traceable to the tool that made it — and the capability stays here for the internal-reference case described above. ## Known limitations - **Generation consumes the user's Doubao quota** (the app reports 「本次生成将 消耗每日免费额度」). Exactly one generation is issued per call; if the plugin cannot confirm a submission it stops rather than retrying, because a blind retry is what once produced duplicate generations. - **The app window is closed and reopened** on the first call, and Doubao must stay running-and-instrumented for the harvest to complete. - The harvest depends on Doubao's own UI markup (`image-box-grid`, `edit_image_download_button`). A Doubao redesign breaks it; the selector surface is deliberately kept to those two names. - The watermark pass only re-encodes PNG. Other formats are saved exactly as downloaded rather than silently recompressed. # DSH Mobile **中文** · [English](README.en.md) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [![listed in awesome-deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--deepseek--harness-4D6BFE?logo=awesomelists&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness) [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness) [![iOS 17+](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-17%2B-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](docs/VERSIONING.md) [![TestFlight](https://img.shields.io/badge/TestFlight-join-0D96F6?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk) [![connector on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-mobile-link?label=connector)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-mobile-link) [![CI](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) 把电脑上的 [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 会话接到 iPhone 上：原生 iOS 客户端、电脑侧连接器、可自建的公网中转。手机与电脑连接同一个 DSH host，看到同一批会话与同一条 消息流；电脑上运行中的任务在锁屏后继续执行，电脑上挂起的提问可在手机上直接回答。 电脑不需要公网 IP，也不需要 VPN。 ![每一步工具调用都摊开 · 不用公网 IP 扫码就连上 · 浏览预览一键下载 · 让它把电脑上的文件发回手机](docs/artifacts/demo/appstore/overview.jpg) > 配图为 App Store 宣传图（8 张中的 4 张，横版拼合），内容出自同一套合成会话：输出是真实 agent > 输出，项目为虚构，`relay.example.com` 是占位符。分张素材与生成方式见 [`docs/artifacts/demo/`](docs/artifacts/demo)。 ## 状态与兼容性 | 组件 | 当前版本 | 分发方式 | |---|---|---| | iOS App | 1.0 | TestFlight 公开测试（[加入](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk)）；需先安装 TestFlight，构建 90 天后过期 | | 连接器 `dsh-plugin-mobile-link` | 0.7.0 | npm | | 中转（DLP v1） | 本仓库 `relay-go/`（Go，`go-0.2.3`） | 自行部署 | 三者的版本组合与发布策略见 [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md)。 表中版本以 **npm 上已发布的为准**（`npm view dsh-plugin-mobile-link version`），不是仓库里 `package.json` 的值。 ## 前提 - 电脑上已安装并可运行 DSH（`dsh web`）。 - 连接器需要 Node.js ≥ 22。 - 自建中转需要一台有公网 IP 的主机（macOS 或 Linux）与 Caddy。 - 从源码构建 App 需要 macOS + Xcode 16 以上；日常使用不需要。 ## 快速开始 ### A. 使用公共中转 1. 手机上安装 App：先装 Apple 的 TestFlight，再用 加入测试。 2. 电脑上安装连接器——**按宿主装**（两种宿主档案独立，装错不会报错，只是连接器不会被加载）： - 命令行 web 版（终端里跑 `dsh web`）：`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link` - 官方桌面版（双击图标打开的应用）：用应用内的插件页，或应用自带的 `dsh` 命令装进 `desktop` 档案 （普通 npm 版 `dsh` 会拒绝该档案，这是官方设计）。宿主形态的识别判据（双击图标启动还是敲命令启动）见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。 3. 登记到中转：`dsh-mobile-link enroll --invite <邀请码> --relay wss://<中转地址>/dsh-link` 4. 让连接器用上这个身份：重启一次宿主（`dsh web`），或在启动时就带上邀请码 （`DSH_MOBILE_LINK_INVITE=<邀请码> dsh web`）。**第 2 步装插件本身不需要重启**——命令行 web 宿主会 自己把新装的插件挂上；桌面版按应用内提示。 5. 手机 App →「扫码配对」，扫描电脑上的二维码：点 DSH 界面**左下角的「移动端连接」**，小窗里就是 二维码与配对码（点「重新生成」才会换；也可用 `node scripts/dev/show-pair-qr.mjs` 在没有界面的环境里出图）。 邀请码为一次性、绑定一台电脑，在 [issue #1](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/issues/1) 领取； 中转地址与邀请码写在同一行。登录后确认手机顶部显示「已连接」，即为成功。故障排查见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。 ### B. 自建中转 自建使用仓库内的 Go 实现（`relay-go/`）。按 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md) §2–§3 在服务器上构建二进制、写入 `build.json` 并安装 `dsh-relay-go.service`；Caddy 路由用 [`relay-go/deploy/Caddyfile.snippet`](relay-go/deploy/Caddyfile.snippet)，由 [`relay-go/deploy/caddy_splice.py`](relay-go/deploy/caddy_splice.py) 插入既有站点块（§4）。 ```bash # 首次部署 sudo systemctl enable --now dsh-relay-go # 建账号 → 铸邀请码 /opt/dsh-relay-go/bin/dsh-relay admin --db /var/lib/dsh-relay/state.db \ account-create --name "<名称>" /opt/dsh-relay-go/bin/dsh-relay admin --db /var/lib/dsh-relay/state.db \ invite-mint --note "<备注>" --count 1 --relay wss://<站点>/dsh-link ``` 铸出的邀请码回到 A 的第 3 步使用。实时负载与每设备流量： `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/stats`（仅监听回环）。限额与运维细节见 [`relay-go/README.md`](relay-go/README.md) 与 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md)。 ## 组件与数据流 ``` ┌──────────────┐ WSS ┌────────────────────┐ WSS ┌───────────────────┐ │ iPhone App ├─────────►│ Relay（公网主机） │◄─────────┤ 电脑侧连接器 │ │ SwiftUI │ │ 鉴权 + 转发 │ │ (DSH 插件) │ └──────────────┘ └────────────────────┘ └─────────┬─────────┘ │ HTTP + WS ┌─────────▼─────────┐ │ dsh web │ │ 127.0.0.1: │ └───────────────────┘ ``` | 组件 | 位置 | 职责 | |---|---|---| | iOS App | 手机 | 会话列表、转写、图片与文件、配对与设备管理 | | 连接器 | 电脑（DSH 插件） | 以 `127.0.0.1` 访问本机 DSH，转成中转帧 | | 中转 | 公网主机 | 鉴权与按 `agentId` 转发；**不解析会话内容** | | DSH host | 电脑 | 会话、agent 与工具的真实执行方 | 产品上只提供经中转这一条连接方式（`dsh://direct` 是 DEBUG-only 的测试通道）。选型与边界见 [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) 与 [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md)。 ## 配置 仓库中出现的 `relay.example.com` 一律是占位符：中转地址属于部署方，不属于仓库。真值只存在于本机， 且均被 gitignore： | 位置 | 用途 | 提供方式 | |---|---|---| | `.env.local` | 发布脚本、开发探针 | `cp .env.example .env.local`，填 `DSH_SITE` / `DSH_RELAY_URL` / `DSH_OTA_HOST` | | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | 连接器的中转地址与身份 | `dsh-mobile-link enroll --invite <码> --relay <地址>` | | `ios/DSHMobile/Config.local.xcconfig` | App 内预填的中转地址与更新源 | 从 `Config.xcconfig` 复制后填写 | 因此直接 clone 构建出的 App 默认连不上任何中转，这是有意设计。 ## 开发 ```bash cd ios/DSHMobile/DSHKit && swift test # 协议层 cd plugins/mobile-link && npm test # 连接器 cd relay-go && make test # 中转（Go，生产实现） cd mail && ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q # 信件服务 npm run check:secrets # 本机真值没有进跟踪文件 npm run check:docs # 文档规范（结构、口吻、链接） cd ios/DSHMobile && xcodebuild -scheme DSHMobile \ -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=DSH-Test' build ``` 上述单测与一次「不带任何本机配置」的 Release 构建由 GitHub Actions 在干净仓库上执行。需要仿真器、 真实中转或开发者团队 ID 的验证不在 CI 内——CI 通过不等于可以发布。 界面测试是一套独立测试台：`./test/run.sh prepare` → `run <用例>` → `report --verdict …`，口径见 [`test/RULES.md`](test/RULES.md)，可复制的用例模板见 [`test/examples/`](test/examples)。 ## 文档 | 文档 | 内容 | |---|---| | [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md) | 两种部署路径的选择、操作步骤、故障排查 | | [`docs/GLOSSARY.md`](docs/GLOSSARY.md) | 术语表（DSH、host、连接器、中转、DLP 等） | | [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | 架构与关键决策 | | [`docs/DSH-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/DSH-PROTOCOL.md) | DSH 原生协议参考（权威、面向实现） | | [`docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md) | DLP v1 中转协议规范 | | [`docs/CONNECTOR-NOTES.md`](docs/CONNECTOR-NOTES.md) / [`docs/RELAY-NOTES.md`](docs/RELAY-NOTES.md) | 实现与规范的偏差记录 | | [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md) | 连接方式与配对设计 | | [`docs/IMAGES.md`](docs/IMAGES.md) | 图片能力的设计约束与实现 | | [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md) | 三处部署的版本与发布策略 | | [`docs/PRIVACY.md`](docs/PRIVACY.md) | 隐私说明：App 不收集数据，中转只做转发 | | [`docs/dsh-rpc-catalog.json`](docs/dsh-rpc-catalog.json) | 某次快照：机器可读的 RPC 目录（不是持续校验的契约） | | [`docs/artifacts/samples/`](docs/artifacts/samples) | 从真实 DSH 抓取的响应样例（已脱敏） | 参与开发见 [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md)，安全问题的报告方式见 [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md)， 版本变化见 [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md)。 ## 已知限制 - **iOS 安装走 TestFlight**：需先安装 Apple 的 TestFlight；测试构建 90 天后过期，到期需安装新构建。 自行部署时也可以走 OTA（部署脚本会生成 `https://<站点>/ios/`）：那用 Ad Hoc 描述文件， 只覆盖已登记 UDID 的设备，适合自己用，不适合公开分发。 - **后台通知覆盖这些场景**：从手机发出任务后把 App 退到后台，任务完成、以及 Agent 提问后 等待回答（App 列表顶部会显示一条待回应提示）这两件事，仍会通知到手机。它只在 「有任务在跑，或有待回答的提问」时生效，空闲时不耗电。 - **这些场景不覆盖**：手机在后台时，电脑端**新开始**的会话唤不起 App（需要 APNs，尚未实现）； 长时间未回答的提问可能丢失。 - 文件发送仅在经中转时可用。 ## 许可 MIT，见 [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)。

# dsh-plugin-mobile-link

[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![listed in awesome-deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--deepseek--harness-4D6BFE?logo=awesomelists&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](../../LICENSE)

> 面向：使用者与实现者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20

**The computer half of [DSH Mobile](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile): it
dials a relay over WSS, so the native iOS client reaches this DSH instance even
though the computer has no public IP.**

```
iPhone App ──WSS──▶ Relay（公网，只鉴权与转发）──WSS──▶ this plugin ──HTTP+WS──▶ 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

The connector always talks to the local DSH as `127.0.0.1:<port>`, so the host's
authority and its trust fence are unaffected: no `--trusted-host`, no rewritten
`Host`, no new listening port on this machine.

```
plugins/mobile-link/
├── package.json          # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch, bin: dsh-mobile-link
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch: the loader row + config reference
├── lib/
│   ├── index.js          # cordis plugin: starts the agent, registers 3 routes
│   ├── link.js           # the DLP agent transport: identity, socket, heartbeat, reconnect
│   ├── router.js         # frames ⇄ local DSH mux streams, per-device `$events`
│   ├── dlp.js            # DLP v1 frame codec (shared with the relay)
│   ├── files.js          # phone → computer file transfers (`_link/file*` methods)
│   ├── enroll.js         # invite-code redemption, writes ~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json
│   ├── journal.js        # lifecycle journal: why a relay link was dropped, after the fact
│   ├── routes.js         # GET /mobile-link/status, POST /pair-code, POST /pair-code/regenerate
│   ├── qr.js             # dependency-free QR SVG
│   └── cli.js            # dsh-mobile-link: enroll / mint-pair-code
└── test/                 # node --test, 100+ tests (no DSH, no network)
```

## Install

The connector runs in whichever host runs your DSH. There are two supported hosts today —
**the official desktop app** and **the command-line web host** — and each keeps its own
profile, so you install the plugin into the one you actually use. The connector discovers
the local DSH by itself in both (the host hands it the authenticated loopback address);
you never type an address or a token.

**Command-line web host**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link
```

**Official desktop app** — install through the app's own plugin page, or with the CLI that
the app ships (`…/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh`, installable from its settings). The npm
`dsh` refuses this profile on purpose (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the
Electron application`). Two prerequisites matter in practice: let the app start once so it
initializes its profile, and **quit it completely** before installing — otherwise the
profile is locked.

```bash
# quoting the app's bundled CLI; see docs/ONBOARDING.md for the section titles
"<DeepSeek Harness.app>/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh" \
  plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-mobile-link
```

Then restart the host (or reload the profile). From a checkout the same command takes
a path — the leading `./` matters, because DSH anchors a relative spec against
your current directory instead of resolving it inside the profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/mobile-link
```

## Use

1. Register this computer with a relay (once). Either redeem an invite code:

   ```bash
   dsh-mobile-link enroll --invite <邀请码> --relay wss://<你的站点>/dsh-link
   ```

   …or register it on the relay host with `dsh-relay admin agent-register
   --write-config ~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json`.

2. Mint a pairing code, and show it as a QR the phone camera can read:

   ```bash
   dsh-mobile-link --mint-pair-code        # prints JSON: code + relay + agentId
   ```

   Or open the **移动端连接** panel at the bottom of the sidebar in the DSH client
   (spec 010) — same persistent code, same QR, shown until you click 重新生成.

3. Scan it in the iOS app. The code can be claimed again for another phone, a reinstall
   or a new device; only 重新生成 revokes it (already-paired devices stay connected).
   After that the phone reconnects on its own — nothing else has to be run by hand.

`GET /mobile-link/status` reports whether the link is up, which devices are
attached, and whether this computer is registered yet. Its `journal` block carries
the current process's newest lifecycle events (link opened/closed with the reason,
device attached/detached); the counters in it reset when the plugin hot-reloads, so
the full history — across restarts — is the JSONL file at `journal.path`.

## Configuration

All optional; the defaults are what a stock deployment needs. Set them in the
plugin's config block (`cordis.patch.yml`), not by editing this file.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` stops the outbound link without uninstalling |
| `relayUrl` | from `agent.json` | Relay base URL; a bare deployment dials `<relay>/link/agent` |
| `agentId` / `agentSecret` | from `agent.json` | Override the enrolled identity |
| `stateFile` | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | Where the identity lives |
| `journalFile` | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/link-events.jsonl` | Lifecycle journal (rotated once at 256 KiB); `false` keeps it in memory only |
| `slowRequestMs` | `2000` | A slower single request gets its own `request.slow` entry; `0` disables those (per-attach `device.summary` is still written) |
| `diagnostics` | `true` | `false` refuses the phone's phase uploads; the phone ignores the refusal and stays connected |
| `dshUrl` | discovery | Explicit local DSH base URL (usually unnecessary — the host hands the connector its own address) |
| `heartbeatMs` | `20000` | DLP ping interval |

The connector does **not** read an endpoint handoff file any more: discovery happens inside
the host process (`ctx.inject(['webServer','connection'])`), which is what makes one npm
package work on both the desktop app and the command-line host. It **writes** one instead —
`$DSH_HOME/mobile-link/endpoint.json`, mode 0600 — for tools that run *outside* the host
(our dev/test scripts and the iOS integration helpers).

Address resolution order: this config block, then `DSH_RELAY_URL` (or
`DSH_MOBILE_LINK_RELAY`), then the enrolled identity file, then the repository
placeholder `wss://relay.example.com/dsh-link` — the placeholder being the
"nothing configured yet" sentinel rather than a real address.

## Design notes

- **No required services.** `inject` is empty and the routes are attached through
  `ctx.inject([...])`, so a future DSH that renames or drops `webServer` /
  `connection` cannot make the tunnel fatal on boot.
- **Protocol-transparent.** Nothing outside `lib/` is imported and no DSH
  business API is touched: the connector forwards frames, it does not interpret
  sessions. The relay has the same property.
- **Disable** by removing the row from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or by
  setting `enabled: false`.

## Test

```bash
cd plugins/mobile-link && npm test    # zero dependencies
```

The wire protocol is specified in
[`docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/blob/main/docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md).

MIT.

> 输出，项目为虚构，`relay.example.com` 是占位符。分张素材与生成方式见 [`docs/artifacts/demo/`](docs/artifacts/demo)。

## 状态与兼容性

| 组件 | 当前版本 | 分发方式 |
|---|---|---|
| iOS App | 1.0 | TestFlight 公开测试（[加入](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk)）；需先安装 TestFlight，构建 90 天后过期 |
| 连接器 `dsh-plugin-mobile-link` | 0.7.0 | npm |
| 中转（DLP v1） | 本仓库 `relay-go/`（Go，`go-0.2.3`） | 自行部署 |

三者的版本组合与发布策略见 [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md)。
表中版本以 **npm 上已发布的为准**（`npm view dsh-plugin-mobile-link version`），不是仓库里 `package.json` 的值。

## 前提

- 电脑上已安装并可运行 DSH（`dsh web`）。
- 连接器需要 Node.js ≥ 22。
- 自建中转需要一台有公网 IP 的主机（macOS 或 Linux）与 Caddy。
- 从源码构建 App 需要 macOS + Xcode 16 以上；日常使用不需要。

## 快速开始

### A. 使用公共中转

1. 手机上安装 App：先装 Apple 的 TestFlight，再用 <https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk> 加入测试。
2. 电脑上安装连接器——**按宿主装**（两种宿主档案独立，装错不会报错，只是连接器不会被加载）：
   - 命令行 web 版（终端里跑 `dsh web`）：`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link`
   - 官方桌面版（双击图标打开的应用）：用应用内的插件页，或应用自带的 `dsh` 命令装进 `desktop` 档案
     （普通 npm 版 `dsh` 会拒绝该档案，这是官方设计）。宿主形态的识别判据（双击图标启动还是敲命令启动）见
     [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。
3. 登记到中转：`dsh-mobile-link enroll --invite <邀请码> --relay wss://<中转地址>/dsh-link`
4. 让连接器用上这个身份：重启一次宿主（`dsh web`），或在启动时就带上邀请码
   （`DSH_MOBILE_LINK_INVITE=<邀请码> dsh web`）。**第 2 步装插件本身不需要重启**——命令行 web 宿主会
   自己把新装的插件挂上；桌面版按应用内提示。
5. 手机 App →「扫码配对」，扫描电脑上的二维码：点 DSH 界面**左下角的「移动端连接」**，小窗里就是
   二维码与配对码（点「重新生成」才会换；也可用 `node scripts/dev/show-pair-qr.mjs` 在没有界面的环境里出图）。

邀请码为一次性、绑定一台电脑，在 [issue #1](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/issues/1) 领取；
中转地址与邀请码写在同一行。登录后确认手机顶部显示「已连接」，即为成功。故障排查见
[`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。

### B. 自建中转

自建使用仓库内的 Go 实现（`relay-go/`）。按 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md)
§2–§3 在服务器上构建二进制、写入 `build.json` 并安装 `dsh-relay-go.service`；Caddy 路由用
[`relay-go/deploy/Caddyfile.snippet`](relay-go/deploy/Caddyfile.snippet)，由
[`relay-go/deploy/caddy_splice.py`](relay-go/deploy/caddy_splice.py) 插入既有站点块（§4）。

```bash
# 首次部署
sudo systemctl enable --now dsh-relay-go

# 建账号 → 铸邀请码
/opt/dsh-relay-go/bin/dsh-relay admin --db /var/lib/dsh-relay/state.db \
    account-create --name "<名称>"
/opt/dsh-relay-go/bin/dsh-relay admin --db /var/lib/dsh-relay/state.db \
    invite-mint --note "<备注>" --count 1 --relay wss://<站点>/dsh-link
```

铸出的邀请码回到 A 的第 3 步使用。实时负载与每设备流量：
`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/stats`（仅监听回环）。限额与运维细节见
[`relay-go/README.md`](relay-go/README.md) 与 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md)。

## 组件与数据流

```
┌──────────────┐   WSS    ┌────────────────────┐   WSS    ┌───────────────────┐
│  iPhone App  ├─────────►│  Relay（公网主机）  │◄─────────┤ 电脑侧连接器       │
│  SwiftUI     │          │  鉴权 + 转发        │          │ (DSH 插件)        │
└──────────────┘          └────────────────────┘          └─────────┬─────────┘
                                                                     │ HTTP + WS
                                                           ┌─────────▼─────────┐
                                                           │ dsh web           │
                                                           │ 127.0.0.1:<port>  │
                                                           └───────────────────┘
```

| 组件 | 位置 | 职责 |
|---|---|---|
| iOS App | 手机 | 会话列表、转写、图片与文件、配对与设备管理 |
| 连接器 | 电脑（DSH 插件） | 以 `127.0.0.1` 访问本机 DSH，转成中转帧 |
| 中转 | 公网主机 | 鉴权与按 `agentId` 转发；**不解析会话内容** |
| DSH host | 电脑 | 会话、agent 与工具的真实执行方 |

产品上只提供经中转这一条连接方式（`dsh://direct` 是 DEBUG-only 的测试通道）。选型与边界见
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) 与 [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md)。

## 配置

仓库中出现的 `relay.example.com` 一律是占位符：中转地址属于部署方，不属于仓库。真值只存在于本机，
且均被 gitignore：

| 位置 | 用途 | 提供方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `.env.local` | 发布脚本、开发探针 | `cp .env.example .env.local`，填 `DSH_SITE` / `DSH_RELAY_URL` / `DSH_OTA_HOST` |
| `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | 连接器的中转地址与身份 | `dsh-mobile-link enroll --invite <码> --relay <地址>` |
| `ios/DSHMobile/Config.local.xcconfig` | App 内预填的中转地址与更新源 | 从 `Config.xcconfig` 复制后填写 |

因此直接 clone 构建出的 App 默认连不上任何中转，这是有意设计。

## 开发

```bash
cd ios/DSHMobile/DSHKit && swift test        # 协议层
cd plugins/mobile-link  && npm test          # 连接器
cd relay-go && make test                     # 中转（Go，生产实现）
cd mail && ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q   # 信件服务
npm run check:secrets                        # 本机真值没有进跟踪文件
npm run check:docs                           # 文档规范（结构、口吻、链接）

cd ios/DSHMobile && xcodebuild -scheme DSHMobile \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=DSH-Test' build
```

## 已知限制

- **iOS 安装走 TestFlight**：需先安装 Apple 的 TestFlight；测试构建 90 天后过期，到期需安装新构建。
  自行部署时也可以走 OTA（部署脚本会生成 `https://<站点>/ios/`）：那用 Ad Hoc 描述文件，
  只覆盖已登记 UDID 的设备，适合自己用，不适合公开分发。
- **后台通知覆盖这些场景**：从手机发出任务后把 App 退到后台，任务完成、以及 Agent 提问后
  等待回答（App 列表顶部会显示一条待回应提示）这两件事，仍会通知到手机。它只在
  「有任务在跑，或有待回答的提问」时生效，空闲时不耗电。
- **这些场景不覆盖**：手机在后台时，电脑端**新开始**的会话唤不起 App（需要 APNs，尚未实现）；
  长时间未回答的提问可能丢失。
- 文件发送仅在经中转时可用。

## 许可

MIT，见 [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)。

# dsh-plugin-send-image

> 面向：使用者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20

**Lets the agent put a picture into the conversation.** A screenshot, the
clipboard, or a file — the host normalizes and persists the bytes, every DSH
client renders it inline, and the user can open it full screen.

Why a plugin is needed at all: DSH's model adapters declare **text-only output**,
so the agent cannot emit an image in its answer. The bytes reach the client
through the Host's attachment service (`ctx.attachments.saveImage`, which
normalizes and persists them) and the returned reference rides on this tool's
**result**, as an image content block — so every client draws the picture inside
the agent's own turn.

Submitting it as a prompt instead — which is what this plugin used to do — is
wrong twice over: a prompt is a **user message**, so the picture looked like
something the user had sent, and it **started a turn**, so the agent answered its
own screenshot. `send-image.mjs --via-prompt` keeps that path for a client that
cannot render tool-result images; nothing here uses it.

```
plugins/send-image/
├── package.json          # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch: the loader row
├── lib/index.js          # cordis plugin: registers the send_image tool
└── test/                 # node --test, 19 tests (no DSH, no network)
```

The tool is a thin shell around
[`skills/send-image/send-image.mjs`](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/blob/main/skills/send-image/send-image.mjs),
which owns the capture quirks (`screencapture`, `pngpaste`, the screen-recording
permission message) and prints one JSON descriptor. Standalone it only
*prepares* — the publishing half needs the Host context this plugin has:

```bash
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --screenshot        # prints the descriptor
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --file ./out/render.png
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --clipboard         # needs pngpaste
```

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-send-image
```

Then restart DSH (or reload the profile). From a checkout a relative spec works
too — the leading `./` matters, because DSH anchors it against your current
directory instead of resolving it inside the profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/send-image
```

## Use

The agent calls `send_image`. Exactly one source per call:

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Path to an image (absolute, or relative to the working directory) |
| `screenshot` | `true` captures the whole screen — the picture contains everything on it |
| `clipboard` | `true` sends the image on the clipboard (needs `pngpaste`) |
| `caption` | Text shown with the picture |

Passing none or several is a readable tool error rather than a schema failure:
source exclusivity is a runtime rule here, so the model is told what to fix.

### You can also take the screenshot yourself

Inside the DSH window, `⌥⌘S` (or the button at the left of the composer) starts a drag-select; the
selected rectangle is **attached to the current conversation as a draft** — you decide whether to send
it. The shortcut only works while the DSH window has focus (no system-wide hotkey), and it can be
rebound under Settings → Shortcuts. `Esc` cancels without leaving a file, and a missing Screen
Recording grant prints where to enable it and which program to restart.

Both supported hosts (the official desktop app and the command-line web host) run the same client
half, shipped in this package. The plugin is hot-pluggable: enabling or disabling it adds or removes
the shortcut, the composer button and its styles in place — no host restart, no page reload.

## Test

```bash
cd plugins/send-image && npm test    # 14 tests, zero dependencies
```

MIT.


铸出的邀请码回到 A 的第 3 步使用。实时负载与每设备流量：
`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/stats`（仅监听回环）。限额与运维细节见
[`relay-go/README.md`](relay-go/README.md) 与 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md)。

## 组件与数据流

```
┌──────────────┐   WSS    ┌────────────────────┐   WSS    ┌───────────────────┐
│  iPhone App  ├─────────►│  Relay（公网主机）  │◄─────────┤ 电脑侧连接器       │
│  SwiftUI     │          │  鉴权 + 转发        │          │ (DSH 插件)        │
└──────────────┘          └────────────────────┘          └─────────┬─────────┘
                                                                     │ HTTP + WS
                                                           ┌─────────▼─────────┐
                                                           │ dsh web           │
                                                           │ 127.0.0.1:<port>  │
                                                           └───────────────────┘
```

| 组件 | 位置 | 职责 |
|---|---|---|
| iOS App | 手机 | 会话列表、转写、图片与文件、配对与设备管理 |
| 连接器 | 电脑（DSH 插件） | 以 `127.0.0.1` 访问本机 DSH，转成中转帧 |
| 中转 | 公网主机 | 鉴权与按 `agentId` 转发；**不解析会话内容** |
| DSH host | 电脑 | 会话、agent 与工具的真实执行方 |

产品上只提供经中转这一条连接方式（`dsh://direct` 是 DEBUG-only 的测试通道）。选型与边界见
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) 与 [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md)。

## 配置

仓库中出现的 `relay.example.com` 一律是占位符：中转地址属于部署方，不属于仓库。真值只存在于本机，
且均被 gitignore：

| 位置 | 用途 | 提供方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `.env.local` | 发布脚本、开发探针 | `cp .env.example .env.local`，填 `DSH_SITE` / `DSH_RELAY_URL` / `DSH_OTA_HOST` |
| `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | 连接器的中转地址与身份 | `dsh-mobile-link enroll --invite <码> --relay <地址>` |
| `ios/DSHMobile/Config.local.xcconfig` | App 内预填的中转地址与更新源 | 从 `Config.xcconfig` 复制后填写 |

因此直接 clone 构建出的 App 默认连不上任何中转，这是有意设计。

## 开发

```bash
cd ios/DSHMobile/DSHKit && swift test        # 协议层
cd plugins/mobile-link  && npm test          # 连接器
cd relay-go && make test                     # 中转（Go，生产实现）
cd mail && ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q   # 信件服务
npm run check:secrets                        # 本机真值没有进跟踪文件
npm run check:docs                           # 文档规范（结构、口吻、链接）

cd ios/DSHMobile && xcodebuild -scheme DSHMobile \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=DSH-Test' build
```

上述单测与一次「不带任何本机配置」的 Release 构建由 GitHub Actions 在干净仓库上执行。需要仿真器、
真实中转或开发者团队 ID 的验证不在 CI 内——CI 通过不等于可以发布。

界面测试是一套独立测试台：`./test/run.sh prepare` → `run <用例>` → `report --verdict …`，口径见
[`test/RULES.md`](test/RULES.md)，可复制的用例模板见 [`test/examples/`](test/examples)。

## 文档

| 文档 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md) | 两种部署路径的选择、操作步骤、故障排查 |
| [`docs/GLOSSARY.md`](docs/GLOSSARY.md) | 术语表（DSH、host、连接器、中转、DLP 等） |
| [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | 架构与关键决策 |
| [`docs/DSH-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/DSH-PROTOCOL.md) | DSH 原生协议参考（权威、面向实现） |
| [`docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md) | DLP v1 中转协议规范 |
| [`docs/CONNECTOR-NOTES.md`](docs/CONNECTOR-NOTES.md) / [`docs/RELAY-NOTES.md`](docs/RELAY-NOTES.md) | 实现与规范的偏差记录 |
| [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md) | 连接方式与配对设计 |
| [`docs/IMAGES.md`](docs/IMAGES.md) | 图片能力的设计约束与实现 |
| [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md) | 三处部署的版本与发布策略 |
| [`docs/PRIVACY.md`](docs/PRIVACY.md) | 隐私说明：App 不收集数据，中转只做转发 |
| [`docs/dsh-rpc-catalog.json`](docs/dsh-rpc-catalog.json) | 某次快照：机器可读的 RPC 目录（不是持续校验的契约） |
| [`docs/artifacts/samples/`](docs/artifacts/samples) | 从真实 DSH 抓取的响应样例（已脱敏） |

参与开发见 [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md)，安全问题的报告方式见 [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md)，
版本变化见 [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md)。

## 已知限制

- **iOS 安装走 TestFlight**：需先安装 Apple 的 TestFlight；测试构建 90 天后过期，到期需安装新构建。
  自行部署时也可以走 OTA（部署脚本会生成 `https://<站点>/ios/`）：那用 Ad Hoc 描述文件，
  只覆盖已登记 UDID 的设备，适合自己用，不适合公开分发。
- **后台通知覆盖这些场景**：从手机发出任务后把 App 退到后台，任务完成、以及 Agent 提问后
  等待回答（App 列表顶部会显示一条待回应提示）这两件事，仍会通知到手机。它只在
  「有任务在跑，或有待回答的提问」时生效，空闲时不耗电。
- **这些场景不覆盖**：手机在后台时，电脑端**新开始**的会话唤不起 App（需要 APNs，尚未实现）；
  长时间未回答的提问可能丢失。
- 文件发送仅在经中转时可用。

## 许可

MIT，见 [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-scrapling

Scrapling web scraping for dsh: JavaScript rendering, structured extraction and a background crawler, behind one resident Python sidecar.

**A web-scraping extension for [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): [Scrapling](https://github.com/D4Vinci/Scrapling) as agent tools — JavaScript rendering, CSS/XPath extraction with self-healing selectors, sessions with login state, a background crawler and page Q&A. You supply the interpreter and the browser engine; everything runs in one resident Python process.** ## Contents - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Install](#install) - [Runtime packs (macOS arm64)](#runtime-packs-macos-arm64) - [Verify it is live](#verify-it-is-live) - [What it does not provide](#what-it-does-not-provide) - [Enabling it in dsh](#enabling-it-in-dsh) - [The tools](#the-tools) - [Replacing the built-in fetch and search](#replacing-the-builtin-fetch-and-search) - [MCP mode](#mcp-mode) - [Settings](#settings) - [Proxies](#proxies) - [Security](#security) - [Data and privacy](#data-and-privacy) - [Known boundaries](#known-boundaries) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Development](#development) - [License](#license) ## What it does dsh ships `web_fetch` and `web_search`. The built-in `web_fetch` is deliberately honest and minimal: a plain HTTP(S) GET with no JavaScript execution and an honest User-Agent. That is a good default — and it means a single-page application yields only its loading shell, and there is no way to ask for "just the product table". Measured on a page whose content exists only after JavaScript runs: | Pipeline | Text obtained | |---|---| | raw HTML to text (no JS) | `SPA Shell / LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` | | `Fetcher` (curl_cffi, still no JS) | `SPA Shell / LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` | | browser render (patchright) | full rendered DOM, Markdown table, structured rows | This package adds what the built-ins structurally cannot do: - **Browser rendering** — JavaScript execution via patchright. - **Structured extraction** — CSS/XPath selection returning data, not a wall of Markdown. - **Self-healing selectors** — Scrapling's `adaptive` mode relocates an element after the site's markup changes; a selector that returns `None` after a class rename returns the relocated element with `adaptive` on. Everything runs against **one long-lived Python process**. That is not an optimisation: Scrapling's session classes keep cookies, the browser engines keep a page pool, and `adaptive` keeps a SQLite fingerprint database — a process per call would throw all of that away. Tools are registered **conditionally**: the plugin probes what the environment can actually do at startup and registers only what will work, so the model never burns a turn on a tool that was guaranteed to fail. Every tool renders its result row through the official tool-call view slot. `scrapling_answer` is the only tool that spends **another model call** — see [The tools](#the-tools). ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @jayyuen66/dsh-scrapling ``` Remove with `dsh plugin --profile web remove @jayyuen66/dsh-scrapling`. The package is on the public npm registry, so installation needs no credentials and no scoped-registry line. - **Requires Node.js `>= 22.12`.** This is an ESM-only package; that Node floor is what makes `require()` of an ESM entry work at all, which is why `engines.node` is declared. - **Requires host `dsh` at the `0.2.1-rc.3` line.** The requirement the host actually reads is `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.1-rc.3`), and it decides alone; a host on a later line is refused and needs the explicit risk grant `dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @ --dsh-version --accept-risk`. - **Requires Python 3.14+ with Scrapling installed** — in the repository's `_env/.venv`, or reachable from `PATH`, or named by `pythonBin`. In an installed package the `_env/.venv` leg does not exist, so the interpreter is the `python3` on your `PATH`; whichever one is chosen is logged at load time, and a missing Scrapling reports an error carrying the install line to copy. ```sh pip install "scrapling[rag]>=0.5,<0.6" python -m patchright install chromium ``` - **Why `rag` and not `fetchers`:** `rag` is `fetchers` plus `markdownify`, and the default `extractionType` is `markdown` — with plain `fetchers` the first fetch raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at the Markdown conversion. - **Version range:** developed and verified against Scrapling **0.5**, through interfaces that are not stable API surface (`Selector`, `Spider`, `SessionManager`, and the converter's noise-stripping helpers). The upper bound is pinned below `0.6`; outside the range the guards still run, but the anti-injection cleaning and the crawl path may not behave as documented. In 0.5 the browser backend is patchright only (the old standalone stealth fetch is gone; its anti-detection arguments live on `scrapling_render`), `capture_xhr` became session-level recording (hence `scrapling_session_network`), and `extra_flags` became additive — this package sends none, and WebRTC leak protection is carried by the `blockWebrtc` switch. - **Without the installer, the browser engine is yours.** The optional CLI can install the verified macOS arm64 set; the plugin itself downloads nothing at load time. Without a browser it simply does not register the browser-dependent tools, so the model never wastes a turn calling them. - **No `@deepseek-ai/*` under `dependencies`, by contract** (`test/publish-manifest.test.ts` enforces it). Consumer profiles install with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, so a host package there becomes a real second copy whose module-level state splits from the running host's — every native tool call then throws while build and tests stay green. The host packages the artifact imports for value are required peers and stay externalized; the gate imports the built artifact and asserts that no host package body is inlined. - **The artifact is ESM-only and never committed** — `prepack` rebuilds it, so what ships is always what the current source produces. ### Shared version floor If your profile pins `@jayyuen66/dsh-plugin-shared` with a pnpm `overrides` entry, that pin must be at least the version this package declares. A lower pin installs a copy without the names the sources use, and the host then reports `N entries did not activate` together with `does not provide an export named ...` at boot - the package installs fine and never loads, and no per-repository CI run can see it. ## Runtime packs (macOS arm64) The package ships `bin/dsh-scrapling.mjs`. It installs the ability packs into `dataDir/runtime` (default `~/.dsh-scrapling`) — never into system Python and never into the user's Playwright cache. There is **no `postinstall`**; nothing is downloaded when the plugin loads. ```sh dsh-scrapling setup --feature core --apply dsh-scrapling setup --feature browser --apply dsh-scrapling setup --status ``` - `core` installs managed Python 3.14.9, Scrapling 0.5 and its pinned wheels; `browser` adds the full Chromium build (not the headless shell). - `search`, `media`, `mcp` and `adaptive-redis` all ride on `core`'s venv: `mcp` brings the official `scrapling-mcp` server (the `mcp` package, 16 tools) that `official-mcp` mode needs, and `adaptive-redis` brings the `redis` client behind `adaptiveStorage: redis`. Every pack is installable; the settings card reports each as `ready`, `missing`, `corrupt` or `installing`. - `--feature` is a dry run by default; `--apply` writes. `--repair` re-installs without touching user data, and `--uninstall [--purge]` removes runtime files; only `--purge` removes `elements_storage.db` and `downloads/`. - `--offline

` installs with no network at all: `` must hold the Python archive named exactly as the manifest URL's last segment (browser and `curl -O` both keep `cpython-3.14.9+…-install_only.tar.gz`, and the percent-encoded spelling is accepted too) plus a `wheels/` directory with one wheel per pinned requirement - `pip download --only-binary=:all: --require-hashes -r py/runtime-requirements.txt -d /wheels` produces it. The hash check on the Python archive is the same one the networked path runs, and pip is invoked with `--no-index`; a missing archive or wheelhouse fails as `INSTALL_OFFLINE_ASSETS` instead of silently going online. - The settings card can start the same install/repair/cancel actions through the `scraplingRuntime` remote when the profile has both a remote surface and a jobs backend; otherwise it prints the CLI command. - `integrationMode` is deployment-only; `setup --mode` prints or writes the client entry for the two MCP shapes and `doctor` checks a profile against it — see [MCP mode](#mcp-mode). `official-mcp` starts `scrapling-mcp` from the managed venv, which the `mcp` pack provisions (`setup --feature mcp --apply`). - Only **macOS arm64** is verified. Windows, Linux and macOS x64 are blocked (B1/B2): every pack reports `blocked` and the installer refuses rather than guessing an asset path. ## Verify it is live 1. **The layer is mounted.** `dsh --profile web --dump-config` shows this package's layer line. - That command is the only accepted "it is in the layer stack" signal, and it is **not read-only** — it rewrites the profile's root assembly file. Read layer lines from stdout **and** check stderr separately: an unmatched patch target appears only on stderr, so the exit code alone proves nothing. Accept both `# == ` and `# == , patched by `. 2. **The startup log names the interpreter and the plan.** One line prints the probed capabilities and how many of the tools registered; the chosen interpreter path is logged at load. An interpreter that starts but lacks Scrapling is named in the log together with the pip line to copy. 3. **The settings card renders.** The plugin detail page carries the **scrapling** card with every user-editable field grouped by purpose; toggling a value enables Save, and the write returns 200. 4. **A tool round-trip.** Ask the model to fetch a JavaScript-heavy page: the result row renders in the chat through the official tool-call view. On a machine without a browser the render / capture_xhr tools are absent from the model's tool list and their prompt guidance is gone too — that absence is the conditional registration working, not a failure. ## What it does not provide - **It is not a search engine.** Discovery runs in the Python sidecar against one of six backends (`searchBackend`: `auto` / `tavily` / `bing` / `brave` / `serper` / `duckduckgo` / `searxng`); Scrapling's own `google_search` option only sets a referer header. Each backend needs its own setting (`tavilyApiKey`, `braveApiKey`, `serperApiKey`, `searxngEndpoint`) — a backend that is selected but not configured reports `SEARCH_AUTH` instead of silently switching to another one. - **The npm tarball bundles no interpreter or browser.** They come from your machine or from the optional CLI installer, which downloads the verified macOS arm64 set into `dataDir/runtime`; missing pieces remove the matching tools instead of being fetched at load time. - **It opens no HTTP route of its own.** The settings card is a host config form; there is no `/api` surface from this package. - **It adds no dsh subcommand.** The package's own `dsh-scrapling` CLI only manages runtime packs. ## Enabling it in dsh - `dsh.bundle.patch` points at `cordis.patch.yml`, whose single registration line is `- id: scrapling` with the **bare package name** — the host scans `dsh.client` on bare package-name entries only. - The client half registers two surfaces: the settings card (on the `plugins.bundle.config` slot, keyed by the bundle package name — the host dispatches `entryKey: pkg.name`, so the card renders on this package's detail page) and one result row per tool on `tool.call.toolview`, drawn with the official tool-call view props. - The settings namespace is the entry id `scrapling`; precedence is settings-card value > registration-line `config:` > schema default. Setting a field back to its default saves a **clear-override**, not a write of the same value, so a later default change still reaches you. - Gate policy and the sidecar environment are snapshotted once when the plugin is applied — **settings changes take effect on the next start**. - Disabling a tool also removes its system-prompt guidance: the guidance is re-read at each prompt assembly against the tools that scope can actually see, so a machine without a browser loses the render / capture_xhr lines and a sidecar that never came up loses all of them. The section is placed next to the built-in `web_fetch` guidance. - `scrapling_crawl` registers its own job kind, so `job_list` labels its jobs as crawls rather than shell jobs. ## The tools Nineteen tools, each behind one settings switch, all exercised by the test suite: | Tool | Backend | Needs a browser | Concurrency | |---|---|---|---| | `scrapling_fetch` | `Fetcher` (curl_cffi) | no | concurrent; write verbs are serialised once `allowWriteMethods` is on | | `scrapling_extract` | `Selector` + CSS/XPath + `adaptive` | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_locate` | text / regex / similar-element lookup; returns generated selectors | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_links` | `LinkExtractor` plus next-page candidates | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_render` | `StealthySession` (patchright) | yes | serialised; the anti-detection switches (`solveCloudflare` / `hideCanvas` / `blockWebrtc`) live here | | `scrapling_capture_xhr` | one throwaway session, page-level recording | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_session_open` / `scrapling_session_fetch` / `scrapling_session_network` / `scrapling_session_state_save` / `scrapling_session_state_load` / `scrapling_session_list` / `scrapling_session_close` | Scrapling session classes | browser sessions only | serialised | | `scrapling_session_read` | current DOM of a browser session page | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_session_act` | structured actions on a session page (deployment gate) | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_download` | byte download into `dataDir/downloads` (deployment gate) | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_screenshot` | PNG/JPEG screenshot handed to the attachment service | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_crawl` | Scrapling Spider framework (`content` / `sitemap` / `feed`) as a job | no | serialised | | `scrapling_answer` | any fetch path plus `ctx.llm` | with `render: true` | serialised | - **Quotas.** At most 8 open sessions (3 of them browser sessions, each a real Chromium process), 2 crawls in flight, per-page bodies clipped by `*MaxOutputChars`, 8 MB per protocol frame, 16 queued frames. A ceiling answers with a specific code (`SESSION_LIMIT` / `CRAWL_BUSY` / `BAD_FRAME`) the model can back off from. - **`scrapling_crawl` returns a job id immediately** — a crawl takes minutes and a tool call has a timeout. Watch it with `job_list`, read it with `job_output`, stop it with `job_kill`; the tool needs a jobs registry that can attach a controller, and a profile without one simply does not register it (single-page fetching is unaffected). The crawl has a wall-clock ceiling (`crawlMaxRuntimeSeconds`) and never leaves the start domain. Politeness defaults follow Scrapling's spider defaults — robots.txt is **not** obeyed, per-domain delay is 0, up to 4 requests run in parallel — and is a deployment decision, not a per-call one (see [Settings](#settings)). - **`scrapling_answer` fetches the page first, then hands the text plus your question to a model** and returns the conclusion instead of the whole page. It follows the model the current session is already using by default (read from the session's live request header, so a mid-session model switch is picked up), which burns no separate quota; pin `answerProvider` / `answerModel` to route page-reading elsewhere. Page text is **untrusted input** — the prompt frames it explicitly as data, but that defence is prompt-level: it lowers the risk, it does not remove it. ### Render or static `scrapling_render` is much slower and heavier than `scrapling_fetch`, so start static. Two criteria: - **If the rendered result is shorter than the static fetch, go back to static.** Plenty of sites ship readable text from the server and then have their own script empty those containers and swap in canvas / Lottie animation — for those pages rendering can only lose content, and no wait setting brings it back. That is site behaviour, not a plugin defect. - **`waitSelector` waits for an element to appear, not for content to settle.** The element can be removed after it matched, so "the selector matched" does not mean the content is in the result. One thing that is not a criterion but worth knowing: axis ticks inside SVG **cannot be fetched at all** — the Markdown conversion emits no ` Replacing the built-in fetch and search The plugin registers itself as a **fetch provider** and a **search provider** on `ctx.web`, so the built-in `web_fetch` / `web_search` tools actually run on Scrapling instead of dsh's plain-HTTP implementation. The model still calls `web_fetch` / `web_search` — tool names cannot be swapped (same-name registration throws), the provider seam is the supported channel. Both providers are registered by default (`provideWebFetch` / `provideWebSearch`), but that alone displaces nothing: 1. leave `provideWebFetch` / `provideWebSearch` at their default (`true`); 2. set `fetchProvider` / `searchProvider` to `"scrapling"` in the **deployment** config. A configured id wins over auto-selection, which is why step 2 is required — and with two usable providers and no id named, `ctx.web` answers `WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS` and the tool becomes unavailable outright. Two consequences of pointing that line at this plugin: - **If the sidecar cannot start, the built-in `web_fetch` reports `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE`** rather than quietly falling back to plain HTTP. - **If you later remove the plugin but leave the line in**, the built-in tools report `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_MISSING` — go back and remove `fetchProvider` / `searchProvider` too. - **The fetch provider really applies the output budget**: a body over `fetchMaxOutputChars` is cut to a head/tail window and flagged `truncated`, not passed through with a flag. Failures keep the sidecar code prefix (`URL_BLOCKED`, `SIDECAR_TIMEOUT`, `SIDECAR_UNAVAILABLE`), so a policy refusal is distinguishable from a crash or a timeout. Search is split in two, because Scrapling is not a search engine: **discovery** runs in the Python sidecar against the backend `searchBackend` names — Tavily, Bing HTML, Brave (API), Serper (API), DuckDuckGo HTML or SearXNG (JSON API); **reading** is this plugin's — the first `searchRenderTopN` results are actually fetched and, with a browser, rendered, so one `web_search` call returns both which pages matter and what they say. `auto` uses Tavily when `tavilyApiKey` is set, otherwise Bing. Only Tavily and Bing have been exercised against the real endpoints here; Brave, Serper, DuckDuckGo and SearXNG are implemented to their documented request/response shapes and verified against local stubs, with real keys and real instances still unverified. Every returned URL goes through the same gate as a fetch; a page that fails to read is skipped alone, because search results routinely contain dead links. One consequence to know: `dsh-web`'s fetch body is a **closed** union of `html | text` with no `markdown` kind, and adding one is a cross-package change a plugin cannot make. The fetch provider therefore reports Scrapling's Markdown as `text`, which the built-in renderer displays normally. Use `scrapling_fetch` directly when you need `html` or a CSS selector. ## MCP mode `integrationMode` selects one of three mutually exclusive tool surfaces. It is deployment configuration (the `config:` block of `cordis.patch.yml`), it is read once when the plugin is assembled, and changing it requires a restart. | Mode | What it registers | |---|---| | `native` (default) | the `scrapling_*` tools listed above | | `mcp` | no native tools; the plugin serves the same tool table over MCP | | `official-mcp` | no native tools and no server from this plugin; `setup` only generates the `dsh-mcp-client` entry for the official `scrapling-mcp`, which runs in its own process, with its own sessions, and **without this plugin's URL guard** | In `mcp` mode the server runs inside the plugin's own host process and calls the same sidecar, so the URL guard, sessions, jobs and adaptive storage are the same ones the native tools use — there is no second implementation to drift. - **Endpoint** `http://127.0.0.1:/mcp` (`mcpPort`, default `39217`). Only loopback is bound; a request whose declared body exceeds 1 MiB is refused with `413`, and any other path gets `404`. The server is stateless: each request gets its own protocol instance, so nothing survives across them. - **Auth** off by default. Set the environment variable `DSH_SCRAPLING_MCP_TOKEN` and every request must then carry `Authorization: Bearer `. The token is only ever read from the environment, never from the profile, so it does not land in a config file. - **Tools** are the same `ToolDefinition` objects native registers: same JSON Schema, same argument validation, same renderers. `scrapling_answer` is not served — it routes through the model of the hosting session, which an external client does not have. `search` exists only on this surface, because an MCP client has no `ctx.web` seam. The gates are identical: with `allowBrowserActions=false` there is no `session_act`, with `allowFileDownloads=false` there is no `download`, and `search` is absent when no search backend is available. - **Results** are text content; a screenshot comes back as MCP image content instead of a host attachment. A failing tool returns `isError` with a readable message rather than dropping the connection. - **Names**: the MCP raw name is the tool name without the `scrapling_` prefix, and dsh's MCP client shows it as `mcp__scrapling__`. | Native tool | MCP raw name | |---|---| | `scrapling_fetch` | `fetch` | | `scrapling_extract` | `extract` | | `scrapling_locate` | `locate` | | `scrapling_links` | `links` | | `scrapling_render` | `render` | | `scrapling_capture_xhr` | `capture_xhr` | | `scrapling_session_open` | `session_open` | | `scrapling_session_fetch` | `session_fetch` | | `scrapling_session_network` | `session_network` | | `scrapling_session_state_save` | `session_state_save` | | `scrapling_session_state_load` | `session_state_load` | | `scrapling_session_list` | `session_list` | | `scrapling_session_close` | `session_close` | | `scrapling_crawl` | `crawl` | | `scrapling_session_read` | `session_read` | | `scrapling_session_act` | `session_act` | | `scrapling_download` | `download` | | `scrapling_screenshot` | `screenshot` | | — (`ctx.web` only) | `search` | Connecting dsh needs `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, which this plugin deliberately does not depend on. Pin the build that matches the current host — npm `latest` is older than the host's own line and the host rejects the mismatch: ```bash dsh plugin --profile add @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.1-rc.3 ``` Then add one entry to that profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — this is exactly what `dsh-scrapling setup --mode mcp` prints, so you can also let the CLI write it (drop `headers` when no token is configured): ```yaml - insert: - id: scrapling-mcp name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client' config: serverName: scrapling transport: streamable-http url: http://127.0.0.1:39217/mcp failOnStartupError: false # only with DSH_SCRAPLING_MCP_TOKEN set: # headers: # Authorization: !!js '`Bearer ${process.env.DSH_SCRAPLING_MCP_TOKEN}`' ``` `mcpPort` and that URL have to say the same thing; after changing the port, re-apply the entry. `failOnStartupError` is `false` here on purpose: the port only starts listening once the plugin has finished handshaking with the Python sidecar, and the client throws its fiber on the **first** failed connect (`Version negotiation probe failed: connect ECONNREFUSED` → the host reports `1 entry did not activate`). Its own reconnect is on by default (500ms backoff, 10 attempts), so a first-attempt refusal is meant to be absorbed - setting this to `true` would let fiber start order decide whether the mode works. The official `stdio` entry keeps `true`: there the client spawns the server itself, so a failed connect is a real failure and should be loud. ### `setup --mode` and `doctor` `setup --mode` writes that entry text; it never edits a profile. Without `--apply` it is a dry run, and with `--apply` it drops the text in `/mcp/.patch.yml` and prints the path - applying it to `cordis.patch.yml` stays your action, because the host offers no safe append API for that file (`dsh --dump-config` rewrites the profile's root config). ```sh dsh-scrapling setup --mode mcp --port 45991 --with-auth --apply dsh-scrapling setup --mode native --apply # a file that deliberately contains no entry dsh-scrapling doctor --mode mcp --profile ``` `doctor` reads what the profile actually says - `cordis.patch.yml` plus that profile's `package.json` - and prints one line per problem: two entries under `serverName: scrapling`, this plugin's entry next to an official `stdio` one, entries that do not match the mode, an entry whose port disagrees with `--port`, a profile without `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` or with it pinned to something other than `0.2.1-rc.3` / `next`, and an official entry while `officialMcpEnabled` is off. Exit `0` is "consistent", `1` names at least one problem, `2` is a bad argument. `integrationMode` itself is a plugin setting the CLI cannot read, so `--mode` is the claim being checked and has to match the deployment. `official-mcp` asks for two separate statements before it produces anything: `officialMcpEnabled: true` in the profile and `--accept-risk` on the command line; missing either one prints `OFFICIAL_MCP_DISABLED` / `RISK_NOT_ACCEPTED` and wr

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-billing-card *DeepSeek balance, live unit prices and the billing window, in your DSH sidebar* ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-web-blueviolet?style=flat-square) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card?style=flat-square)](https://npmx.dev/package/@jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-yellow?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![](https://img.shields.io/npm/unpacked-size/@jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card?style=flat-square)](https://npmx.dev/package/@jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card) [![](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card/ci.yml?style=flat-square&label=tests)](https://github.com/jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered_by-dsh-4D6BFE?style=flat-square&logo=deepseek&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) [Features](#features) • [Screenshots](#screenshots) • [Installation](#installation) • [How it works](#how-it-works) • [Limits](#limits) • [Development](#development)
A card in the DSH sidebar footer: the balance, the provider and model behind it, their unit prices, and the current billing period with a countdown to the next switch. ## Features - **Balance** — the DSH account balance (recharge + bonus) or the DeepSeek open-platform balance behind your API key, whichever the selected provider bills; it follows the provider in the composer. - **Row per fact** — the provider names the row above the model, so you can see which channel the price belongs to. - **Unit prices** — input, cached and output for the selected model, in the tier active now; no price when another provider serves the model. - **Billing period** — green `Idle` / yellow `Peak`; the countdown to the switch sits top-left, keeps its `Peak in` / `Idle in` wording and takes the period's colour. - **Holidays** (Chinese UI) — a blue strip with the holiday's name, and a gray `调休` (*Make-up*) chip on a make-up workday. - **Currency by language** — CNY prices in Chinese, USD everywhere else. - **Theme and locale** — light and dark themes from the card's own token layer, zh/en dictionaries, built-in data when an upstream cannot be fetched. ## Screenshots Real render, 256 px sidebar at 2× density. ## Installation The package is published on npm ([`@jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card`](https://npmx.dev/package/@jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card)) as a DSH bundle. Use the profile you actually run (`desktop` for the desktop app, `web` for `dsh web`): Requires DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 or newer — `package.json` declares the range in `engines.dsh`, and the manifest fields, the footer slot, and the `locale` and `webServer` services it uses all exist in that release. ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card ``` The same as **Install from npm** on the DSH plugin page. Refresh the GUI afterwards — the card appears at the bottom of the sidebar and hides itself when the sidebar is collapsed to the icon rail. > [!IMPORTANT] > A plugin's Host half loads once per application start, so **restart the application after installing or upgrading**. Until then the card runs on its built-in data. Requires a DSH build with the Web GUI, the sidebar footer slot and the account service. To uninstall: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web remove @jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card ``` ## How it works The Host half fetches both price tables and the China mainland holiday calendar once per application start and serves them on `GET /deepseek-billing-card/data`; the Client half is a React component in `sidebar.footer.action` that reads that route, follows the composer's model picker, and refreshes the balance every 30 s. Switching to the provider that bills the open platform asks the Host for a fresh balance at once, so the amount follows the switch instead of the next tick. ### Billing window Peak is Beijing time, Monday to Friday, 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00, excluding Chinese statutory holidays; everything else is idle. ### Currency A Chinese UI quotes the CNY page, every other language the USD page. Nothing is converted; the balance keeps its wallet currency. ### Hover text Each row's trigger is the thing the row is about: the balance amount itself (help cursor, **no** underline — the number is already the loudest element on the card, and a dashed rule under it reads as a link), the model name (dashed, so the affordance is visible), and the chips (the period always, `Make-up` in the Chinese UI), each with the help cursor. The model bubble belongs to the official price list only: with another provider the numbers are a reference, not that provider's rates. Each bubble is a definition list drawn by the card itself — no host primitive, so it follows the theme instead of inheriting a fixed dark plate: one `label → value` row per fact with a green dot for recharge money and an amber dot for bonus money, then a rule and a quiet footnote. - **Balance** — what the headline adds up to: recharge, bonus, and how often it is re-read. The open-platform balance reads the same way and never mentions the account. - **Model** — a price quote needs four facts, so it states four: the model id, the unit, the snapshot date, and how those numbers were obtained (`startup` or `snapshot`). The period chip lists the peak window (Monday–Friday `09:00-12:00`, then `14:00-18:00`), everything the peak leaves idle, and where the calendar comes from; in the Chinese UI the `Make-up` chip says how a make-up workday is billed (idle all day, like a weekend). No bubble repeats a number the card already shows. The price block and the holiday banner have no hover text — their text already says what they are. The bubble waits 240 ms, flips below the trigger when there is no room above, and closes on leave, blur, or `Esc`. ### Data sources | What | Source | | --- | --- | | Account balance, model | DSH account service; the composer's model selection | | Open-platform balance | `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance`, authorised with the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` credential the Models page stores (the launch environment is the fallback) | | Prices | and | | Holidays | | ## Limits - Prices and holidays are read once per application start; the open-platform balance is re-read every 30 s. A provider switch re-reads it right away. - Without a `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` the card shows the account balance; signed out of the DSH account it shows the open-platform balance instead of a blank. - A model served by a provider other than DeepSeek's own shows no price. - Verified end to end on DSH 0.2.1-rc.3; against 0.2.0-rc.1 the source surface is the same, though that build does not read `engines.dsh` yet. - The card needs the HTTP GUI (`dsh web`); without a web server it runs on the built-in copies, and without the `uiSession` / `modelDirectories` services it prices the catalog default. ## Development No build step: `client.js` is a hand-written browser module, `index.js` and `parse.js` are the Host half. The card renders only its own subtree and resolves every colour from its own `--dbc-*` layer, so it follows the app's light/dark setting without reading a host variable. ``` package.json # dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client cordis.patch.yml # inserts the dsh-billing-card entry index.js parse.js # Host half: startup fetch + the data route client.js # Client half: the card and its built-in fallbacks locale/ # zh/en dictionaries for the plugin manager icon.svg # plugin icon CHANGELOG.md # release notes, English and Chinese, newest first CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md docs/ # README icon, banners, screenshots and the design audit (repo only, not shipped) test/ # offline suite: parsers, host route, client render AGENTS.md # working spec for agents on this repo (repository only, not shipped) .agents/skills/ # project skills for agents on this repo (repository only, not shipped) .github/workflows/ # ci (tests) and publish (npm with provenance) ``` To run a local checkout instead of the published package, add the folder — it is linked into the profile, so `client.js` edits show up on a page refresh: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-billing-card ``` `npm test` runs the offline suite: the parsers against the pages captured in `test/fixtures`, the Host route with a stubbed upstream, and the Client half in a miniature React runtime. No dependencies, no network. `AGENTS.md` holds the working spec, and `.agents/skills/` holds the four project skills for agents. Released under the [MIT license](LICENSE).

# GrokBot Loop

**Interruptible dual-lane agent-loop plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Harness) (dsh).**

> **Disclaimer:** Community homage naming only. **Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by xAI or Grok Bot.** Independent MIT-licensed plugin that replaces the stock `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` Cordis row by id.

English | [中文](./README.zh.md)

## What it does

| Behavior | Stock `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` | GrokBot Loop |
|---|---|---|
| Busy Enter → `steer()` | Waits for current step boundary | **Cooperative cancel** → new step claims user text |
| Mid-stream user steer | Parks until step ends | Abort active stream (**keeps streamed prefix**) + claim |
| Cmd/Ctrl+Enter → `followup()` | next-turn Queue | Same (QueueDock complementary path) |
| Silent `inject()` / tool continue | next-step, no wake | Same (agent lane; no preempt) |
| Trajectory / usage / tools | Full | Same session + `agent/*` contracts |
| Uninstall patch | — | Restores stock loop |

**Dual lanes**

- **User lane** — `steer` / human (and Queue via `followup`): always highest priority.
- **Agent lane** — tool-continue / silent `inject`: only proceeds when the user lane is empty at claim time; never preempts.

## Install (Git URL alone)

Requires a working dsh profile (Node `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0`, dsh `>=0.2.0 <0.3.0`). Peers resolve from the dsh installation (`@deepseek-ai/*` **0.2.1-rc.3** line — see `package.json`).

```sh
# Preferred: activate as a profile bundle (declares dsh.bundle.patch)
dsh plugin --profile web add github:jqlong17/grokbot-agent-loop

# Or npm/pnpm into the profile, then ensure cordis.patch swaps id agent-loop
pnpm --dir "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" add github:jqlong17/grokbot-agent-loop
```

The package ships `cordis.patch.yml` that replaces Cordis id `agent-loop`:

```yaml
- id: agent-loop
  name: '@harness-plugins/grokbot-agent-loop'
  config:
    maxParallelToolCalls: 10
    interruptOnSteer: true
    steerFoldHint: true
    steerFoldMode: bot-like
    steerResumeAnchor: true
    rpwuEnabled: true
    rpwuOtherMode: spawn   # 0.2.0 default (fold = compat)
    rpwuSubagentProvider: spawn
    rpwuSubagentDelivery: caller
    rpwuCheckpointStore: memory
    deliveryGate: true
    deliveryGateMaxRetries: 2
    agents: []
```

See [`examples/cordis.patch.yml`](./examples/cordis.patch.yml) and [`docs/ideal-topology.md`](./docs/ideal-topology.md).

### Manual profile patch

If you install without the bundle layer, add the snippet above to:

`~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`

### Uninstall / restore stock loop

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @harness-plugins/grokbot-agent-loop
```

Or delete the `agent-loop` override from your profile patch so `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`’s stock `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop'` wins again.

## Busy Enter vs Queue shortcut

1. Set Web **Busy Enter** preference to **Steer** (插话) so plain Enter calls `agent.steer()`.
2. GrokBot Loop then **preempts** the live step instead of waiting or QueueDock-parking.
3. **Cmd/Ctrl+Enter** still calls `agent.followup()` → **next-turn Queue** (documented complementary path).

Config flags:
- `interruptOnSteer` (default `true`) — set `false` for stock steer wait semantics
- `steerFoldHint` (default `true`) — after preempt, inject a producer notice: fully answer the newest interrupt, then finish the prior unfinished task without omission (prompt-layer fold vs grok.com Bot; does not rewrite user interrupt text)
- `steerFoldMode` (default `bot-like`) — `bot-like` full two-phase copy; `minimal` shorter notice, same ordering contract
- `steerResumeAnchor` (default `true`) — embed a truncated unfinished MAIN user quote in the fold notice so the model resumes the exact prior deliverable in visible chat; set `false` for 0.1.4-style notices
- `rpwuEnabled` (default `true`) — RPWU WorkUnit registry + step checkpoints + fold-into-unit; set `false` for ≈0.1.5 behavior
- `rpwuOtherMode` (default **`spawn`**, breaking in 0.2.0) — ideal path: host `ctx.subagents.startActivation` for a child Session; `fork`/`subagent` aliases; **`fold`** = explicit 0.1.x short-protocol compat. Missing seam → `[grokbot-unit-fork-degraded]`, never throws
- `rpwuSubagentProvider` (default `spawn`) — provider name for `startActivation`
- `rpwuSubagentDelivery` (default `caller`) — plugin awaits result and folds
- `rpwuCheckpointStore` (default `memory`) — `file` enables FileCheckpointStore skeleton
- `deliveryGate` / `deliveryGateMaxRetries` — unchanged

### Ideal Topology (0.2.1 — main path wired)

```
User/steer → Orchestrator.admit (absorb|spawn|cancel|queue)
                → TurnRunShell (checkpointChain + turn-settle)   ← live
                → ActivationManager (start/wait/cancel/degrade) ← live spawn
                → CheckpointStore (DurableWorkflow seam)
                → MergeBus + DeliveryGate → MAIN chat
```

**0.2.1:** Agent is Cordis host glue; admitted turns run through **TurnRunShell**; spawn/host parallel through **ActivationManager** (missing seam → visible degrade, never throws). Orchestrator remains the only admit brain. Spec: [`docs/ideal-topology.md`](./docs/ideal-topology.md).

**Outer** = this plugin (admit, durability, merge, gate, AgentEvent). **Inner** = dsh ReAct. True parallel = host subagent.

**Breaking vs 0.1.9 (from 0.2.0):** default `rpwuOtherMode` `fold` → `spawn`; package layout split under `orchestrator/` `unit/` `checkpoint/` `merge/` `delivery/` (root re-exports kept). Interruptible ⊥ Durable tested separately.

### 0.1.9 notes

**P1.5 subagent-backed true parallel** (follow-up to 0.1.8 / PR #6). Spec: [`docs/rpwu-p15-subagent-parallel.md`](./docs/rpwu-p15-subagent-parallel.md).

- `rpwuOtherMode: fork|subagent` calls `ctx.subagents.startActivation` so OTHER runs on a **child Agent + child Session** while MAIN keeps its live turn (parent is not cancelled).
- Sibling WorkUnit gains `childSessionId` / `activationRef`; settle → `foldSiblingIntoMain` / peer packet + DeliveryGate.
- Missing host seam → visible `[grokbot-unit-fork-degraded]` + 0.1.8 registry-only cancel-then-claim (no crash).
- Default `fold` short-protocol unchanged.

Honest limit: parallel means **parent Session + child Session via host subagent** — not Temporal, not same-Agent dual LLM kick. Mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent` + `dsh-subagent-spawn-in-process` (optional fork-in-process) in the profile.

### 0.1.8 notes

RPWU P1 slice toward Grok Bot–like work mode (community homage; **not** affiliated with xAI):

- **P1-a fold|fork** — `rpwuOtherMode: fold|fork` (default `fold`). Fork creates a sibling WorkUnit (status / checkpoint / lane queryable via `workUnits.query` / `siblingsOf`); `foldSiblingIntoMain` folds the result back into user-facing MAIN without inventing Temporal.
- **P1-b agent-lane peer return** — `acceptPeerHandoff` models background/peer finished → structured packet (`theme` / `keyPoints` / `todos`) → fold into MAIN conversation (`[grokbot-peer-handoff]`).
- **P1-c deliverySpec** — optional `{ shape, sink }` on WorkUnit; DeliveryGate verifies the contract when present; sticky `chatPosted` + `workspaceOnly` from 0.1.7 unchanged for units without a spec.

Honest limit (closed in 0.1.9 for the fork path): 0.1.8 fork was registry-level sibling bookkeeping inside one Agent session.

### 0.1.7 notes

DeliveryGate substantive delivery: `text + tool` with progress-only narration (no code fence / short body) stays `workspaceOnly` so the gate still fires; sticky `chatPosted` from an earlier OTHER answer no longer skips MAIN tool dumps (`workspaceOnly` also gates). Default `deliveryGateMaxRetries` raised to **2**. Gate notice asks to paste MAIN code/progress into the visible reply.

### 0.1.6 notes

RPWU P0: in-memory WorkUnit registry, step checkpoints on step/end + preempt, fold-into-unit (unitId + goal in fold notice), DeliveryGate (≤1 chat continuation when `chatPosted` is false).

### 0.1.5 notes

MAIN resume anchor on preempt: fold notice quotes the unfinished human MAIN (≤1200 chars) and tightens chat dual-delivery (OTHER then MAIN in the same visible assistant reply; workspace-only ≠ done).

### 0.1.4 notes

Chat-inline dual delivery in fold notice: prefer completing OTHER then unfinished MAIN in the same visible chat/conversation reply; do not treat workspace/tool-only writes as done unless the user asked to save files.

### 0.1.3 notes

Stronger fold copy (never imply dropping the prior task); fixed claim order human→fold; `lastSteerPreempt` trajectory meta; `steerFoldMode`.

## Architecture

Fork of the official agent-loop (MIT) with a thin dual-lane **Scheduler** and interruptible **steer** admission:

1. `decideAdmission('steer', { busy })` → preempt + next-step claim.
2. Driver: cooperative `cancel({ kind: 'user' }, { keepInbox: true })` → enqueue next-step → latch wake.
3. `AgentFactory` (`create` / `resume`) unchanged vs stock — same session persistence and UI events.

Pure scheduler is unit-tested; loop contracts covered by vitest against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers.

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm test          # build + vitest
npm run smoke     # entry + scheduler dry-run
```

## Intentional v1 non-goals

- Temporal / durable cloud runner
- Changing dsh `Phase` to allow same-Agent multi-kick
- Embedding a subagent backend inside this plugin
- Claiming to be an official Grok Bot product

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE) and [NOTICE](./NOTICE) (upstream agent-loop attribution).
