# Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

# Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | # Wework Core DSH terminal runtime This first-party Core DSH plugin owns Wework's local interactive PTY sessions. The packaged Wework frontend calls its same-origin HTTP/SSE API at `/wework/terminal/v1`. The executor remains responsible for task, Codex, local-device and cloud-device execution. It does not proxy desktop terminal input or output. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

    never shipped. OFL condition 5 applies to this package: the font's reserved

    CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Credits and the list of changes we made are in NOTICE
    section 2. Three consequences you must respect:

      BY — keep the credits. Attribution goes to the character's author 上善无形
           (original character 溟月), the DeepSeek-element second pass by
           ZipZipPipe (GPT Image 2), and the refined repair by QYQCAMIAO.
      NC — no commercial use. Ads, sponsorship, paid distribution and paid
           products all count, whether or not you charge for this package.
      SA — share alike. brand-mark-dark.png is a derivative (see NOTICE), and any
           adaptation or derivative you distribute must carry the same licence.

2.3 Wallpapers — NOT distributed, hotlinked
    Since 2026-10-09 (D79) this repository distributes no wallpaper
    image, and since D81 the tracked manifest names the pictures by URL rather than
    leaving the layer empty. Both background images are third-party artwork, not
    ours, and we grant no licence in them. What this repository holds is an address
    and a credit, in two files:

      build/wallpapers.json      TRACKED. Two entries, each with a `direct:` URL
                                 and the `page:` its credit belongs on. The build
                                 emits url("https://…"), so a theme built from
                                 this file paints two pictures the browser fetches,
                                 at paint time, from the host each entry names. No
                                 image bytes travel with it, and an offline machine
                                 simply has no background.
      out/wallpapers.local.json  LOCAL, ignored by git. The same shape with
                                 `dataUrl:` entries; when it exists the build
                                 embeds those local copies instead, which is how
                                 the maintainer's own machine keeps its look.
                                 `--public` ignores it.
      client.js                  GENERATED, ignored by git. `npm run selfcheck`
                                 asserts that the tracked manifest carries no
                                 `dataUrl:` (wall.6) and that a bundle built from
                                 it resolves every `direct:` URL (wall.8). An empty
                                 manifest is still legal: it publishes
                                 `--cp-pick-light: none; --cp-pick-dark: none;`.

    Provenance, recorded because it is the maintainer's own record and because it
    is what a takedown request would be about:

      og33jl — wallhaven.cc/w/og33jl, 2560x1440, credited there to the artist YOTA
               SAKI; the entry's source link is pixiv.net/en/artworks/133258822.

                  uploader; the same artwork also circulates on wallhaven as
                  x85po3, uploaded there by "BachoWilson". haowallpaper serves this
                  preview to anonymous visitors, so the 3066x2160 original — which
                  the maintainer holds, and which this file does not point at — is
                  behind a signed-in download. Not licensed to us.

    entry gone, ask and it will be dropped from the manifest. See README, "Fan work
    and attribution", which also keeps the maintainer's standing notice about images
    taken from the web.

------------------------

  client.js ......................................... MIT (generated from src/, not tracked)
  build/great-vibes-latin.woff2 ..................... OFL 1.1 (2.1)
  build/great-vibes-OFL.txt ......................... OFL 1.1 text
  build/brand-mark*.png, build/brand-mark.jpg ....... CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (2.2)
  the wallpaper pair ................................ NOT distributed, hotlinked (2.3)

Vendored code. Two files are byte-for-byte copies of code from other plugins, not
written for this theme:

  build/plugin-toggle.js ....... dsh-disable-unofficial-plugins, MIT
                                 https://github.com/WhatCannotBeSaid/dsh-disable-unofficial-plugins
  build/session-eva-status.js .. dsh-session-eva-status v0.1.0, MIT
                                 https://github.com/WhatCannotBeSaid/dsh-session-eva-status

Both upstreams are MIT, whose notice has to travel with copies and substantial
portions. NOTICE section 3 carries both entries, and the MIT text with its
copyright line is section 1 of this file. The two files are also inlined into the
generated client.js, so that notice belongs with the bundle and not only with the
two source files. Keep it if you redistribute either file or the bundle.

The CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 legal text for section 2.2 ships with this repository as
LICENSE-CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.txt; the canonical copy is
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/legalcode

No `EVA`, `NERV`, `Evangelion` or Arknights artwork owned by khara, inc. or
Hypergryph is distributed in this package. The only images this repository
carries are the brand marks in 2.2 — both wallpapers are absent as bytes by
construction (2.3), which keeps only their addresses and their credits. The theme
is an unofficial, non-commercial fan work, published under
khara's fan-work guideline (https://www.khara.co.jp/guideline/), which permits
non-commercial fan works and licenses neither the characters nor the brand. See
README, "Fan work and attribution".

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# EVA-Inspired-Theme

[![Licence: MIT + CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT%20%2B%20CC--BY--NC--SA%204.0-yellow.svg)](#licence)
[![Unofficial fan work](https://img.shields.io/badge/project-unofficial_fan_work-blue.svg)](#fan-work-and-attribution)

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A Neon Genesis Evangelion–inspired skin for **DeepSeek Harness**. Two fully
designed modes over one removable override layer, a wallpaper paint layer whose
alphas are solved against a contrast budget rather than picked by eye, and a boot
mask.

This repository ships **no background picture of its own**: the paint layer is
here, the artwork is not. Instead the tracked wallpaper manifest names two
third-party pictures by URL, so a clone draws a background the browser fetches
from those hosts at paint time. The only pictures in git are the brand marks and
the two preview screenshots, which naturally show the art the app was painting;
the theme's look is otherwise unchanged — the alphas, the boot mask, the brand
mark and the fonts all come from this repository.

**Unofficial fan work.** Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or licensed by
khara, inc., Hypergryph, or DeepSeek. See
[Fan work and attribution](#fan-work-and-attribution).

## Preview

Both modes, captured from a running DeepSeek Harness with this package mounted.
The session list is hidden in both shots; nothing else is retouched.

**Title Card — light**

![Title Card, the light mode](docs/preview-light.jpg)

**Central Dogma — dark**

![Central Dogma, the dark mode](docs/preview-dark.jpg)

The backgrounds are the theme's two third-party pictures — what a clone fetches
at paint time. The light shot was taken before the light default moved to its
page on haowallpaper.com (D83), so that one shows an earlier, lower-resolution
upload of the same artwork; the dark shot is the picture the manifest still
names. Credits are in [Fan work and attribution](#fan-work-and-attribution).

## What it is

| | |
|---|---|
| Modes | **Title Card** (light) and **Central Dogma** (dark) |
| Token layer | 55 measured overrides (41 in the light arm, 14 in the dark arm) on a single removable layer |
| Wallpaper layer | No artwork ships in this repository; the browser fetches it at paint time. The tracked manifest points at two third-party pictures — the light default on haowallpaper.com, the dark one on wallhaven — and the maintainer's own machine embeds local copies instead. Surface alphas are solved against a WCAG contrast budget |
| Boot mask | Plays once per DSH launch — the mark lives in sessionStorage, so a reload inside one run does not replay it and quitting DSH does; `?boot=0` skips one, `?boot=1` forces one. Timings and look unchanged |
| Brand mark | One monochrome SVG illustration, drawn at 28×28 inside the 36×36 slot beside the wordmark |
| Composer row | The model and effort triggers carry no chevrons; on a narrow row both become 28×28 icon buttons level with the add and dictation buttons, and the whole row shares one seam (6px wide, 3px narrow) |
| Also inside | A plugin on/off switch and a session-row status rail, both vendored from MIT plugins; a pin button on every workspace and session row; a switch for the WeChat workspace on the workspace row, shown only while WeChat holds an account |
| Language | All user-facing text goes through the official locale service (zh / en) |

The theme installs one layer and can be removed as one. It ships **no settings panel
of its own** — the look is fixed, not a preference — and the only thing it persists
is the workspace pin set. It does hide and move a few official entries, so read
[What it changes in the interface](#what-it-changes-in-the-interface) before you
install it.

## What it changes in the interface

Removing the package takes the layer away again and every official element comes
back. In between, the theme **hides six official entries, rewrites the sidebar
identity line, replaces one page's heading, and reshapes the composer's control
row**. All of it is CSS plus a few client effects — the official DOM is never
rewritten — but here is where things went.

### The brand row is three click zones

The sidebar brand row reads **[illustration] WHALE-01 [SYSTEM]**; the official
wordmark and its whale glyph are hidden. It is one official button carrying three
zones, decided from the click's x coordinate at click time:

| Click | Opens | Because |
|---|---|---|
| the illustration, left of `WHALE-01` | **Plugins** | the 「插件」/ “Plugins” nav row is hidden |
| the `WHALE-01` text | a **new session** | official behaviour, unchanged |
| the `SYSTEM` chip, right of `WHALE-01` | **Settings** | the 「设置」 row and its launcher button are hidden |

The zones drive the hidden buttons programmatically, so both still open. A Plugins row
that your composition does not have is not intercepted at all — the click falls
through to the official new-session handler instead of becoming a hole. Keyboard
activation (Enter or Space on the focused button) and any click held with a modifier
key are left alone. Collapse the sidebar to a rail and there is no brand button, so
there are no zones either.

While the DeepSeek account plugin is enabled it puts an account card into the
Settings slot, in place of the official Settings button. The theme takes that card
out of the layout entirely — no placeholder, no leftover gap — and `SYSTEM` stays
the one Settings entry on the row. Because the card is gone, the click no longer
goes through a synthesised keystroke (a dead click on the desktop build); it asks the
host's shortcut registry to open settings, which is the door that build answers.

### Hidden official entries

| Entry | Where | Way back |
|---|---|---|
| 「应用」/「编辑」 title-bar menu | desktop shell only; absent in a browser | none from inside the app: 关于 / 检查更新 / dsh 命令 / 退出应用 go with it. Quit is still on the tray menu. |
| the second 「新会话」 button | sidebar, below the brand row | `WHALE-01`, or `Ctrl+N` — it is a duplicate |
| 「插件」/ “Plugins” nav row | sidebar | click the illustration; **no shortcut is left** |
| 「设置」 row and its launcher button | sidebar | click `SYSTEM`, or `Ctrl+,` |
| 「收起侧栏」 button | left sidebar only; the right sidebar's stays visible | the collapse command itself is untouched |
| the session list's bottom fade | sidebar | it only dimmed the last row |
| the account card (only while the DeepSeek account plugin is enabled) | sidebar, in the Settings slot | removed outright, with no gap left where it stood; `SYSTEM` still opens Settings |

Where a way back names a keyboard shortcut, that is the desktop default — `Ctrl+N` for
a new session, `Ctrl+,` for settings, both of them the official ones, unchanged by this
theme. The web build binds the same two commands to `Ctrl+Alt+N` and `Ctrl+Alt+,`.

Nothing else in the sidebar moves. The workspace and session list keeps the official
`flex: 1` scrolling area, and the bottom area still shows whatever a third-party
plugin registers into `sidebar.footer.action` (a ledger card, say) in the position the
host gives it.

### The nav area sits under the title bar (desktop shell only)

The first nav button is level with the 对话 / 轨迹 tab row of the main area instead of
sitting below it, and the Settings row moves underneath the nav instead of above it.
That is the one visible reordering in the sidebar, and it applies to the desktop shell
only — the browser build has no title-bar strip to align to, so its layout stays the
one the host draws.

### The new session page (hero)

Three changes, on that page only:

- the headline is replaced by one fixed German line, exactly as registered:
  `Wovon man nicht sprechen kann, darüber muss man schweigen`;
- the 「预览版」/ “Preview” badge is gone;
- the whale logo above the headline is gone.

That line is set in **Great Vibes** (SIL OFL 1.1, shipped in the package) at
`min(44px, 5.3cqw)` and never wraps. Two costs, stated plainly: it is injected as
generated content, so find-in-page and screen readers do not see it, and it does not
follow the interface language — a Chinese and an English user both read the German.

### The composer's control row

The row above Send belongs to the host; the theme only reshapes it.

- The **model** and **effort** triggers carry no disclosure chevron. Their open state
  is already the trigger's own highlight, so the arrow only repeated it.
- The **permission** trigger loses its arrow as well, and gains back the right padding
  the arrow was holding. Its word is its state — the label changes with the level — so
  nothing is lost by dropping the arrow.
- On a narrow row both triggers become 28×28 icon buttons: same box, same ink as the
  add and dictation buttons beside them. A wide row keeps the text labels.
- The whole row shares one seam — 6px when it has room, 3px when it does not — so the
  four controls read as one strip instead of four drifting groups.

The four official popovers that hang off that row — permission, session stats, token
usage and the context meter — are centred on their triggers instead of left-aligned
with them. The sidebar's own view-options menu is left where the host puts it.

### What the theme adds

- A **pin button** on every workspace and session row (置顶工作区 / Pin workspace,
  following the host's language). The pinned set is kept in browser storage under
  `eva-theme/workspace-pins`; the order it produces is written through the host's own
  insert-before API, so it survives a restart — and, unlike the pin set, it also
  survives removing the theme. On the workspace row it sits in the row's own action
  group, so it takes the same 15px seam as the two official buttons beside it.
- The vendored **non-official plugin switch**, on the installed group's header in the
  official Plugins page: tick which non-official plugins to disable, or to enable
  again. It switches bundle enablement only — it installs and uninstalls nothing.
- The vendored **session status rail**: blue and breathing while a session waits for
  you (an approval, a question, a plan review), red while it is the one open in the
  main area, purple while it finished unread. A pinned row gets a rainbow title
  instead of a rail.
- The **boot mask** once per DSH launch (the mark lives in sessionStorage: a reload
  inside one run does not replay it, quitting DSH does; `?boot=1` forces a replay,
  `?boot=0` skips one).

Settings themselves remain the official dialog. The single change there is that the
dim tint behind it is removed; the panel and click-outside-to-close are untouched.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with a web profile.
- Node.js >= 18 — only for the build and check tools. The theme itself runs in
  the browser.

## Install

From npm — a versioned tarball with the browser bundle already built in:

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add eva-inspired-theme
```

Straight from the public repository, which tracks its default branch:

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:WhatCannotBeSaid/eva-inspired-theme
```

The package carries a `prepare` script that runs exactly that build, so an
install straight from the Git URL produces the bundle for you before the package
is linked; the npm tarball ships `client.js` ready-made and runs no build. From a
local checkout or a clone of it:

```
npm run build                                              # writes the browser bundle
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<path-to-this-checkout>
```

Run the build once after cloning: `client.js` is generated and deliberately not
tracked (see [Layout](#layout)). A plain `git clone` needs one build — `npm run
build`, or any `npm install` inside the checkout, which triggers `prepare`. A
clone builds the tracked form: the paint layer points at the two pictures named
in `build/wallpapers.json` and the browser fetches them, so the background needs
a network and the host learns the viewer's IP. That is the intended public form.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the profile reconciles its bundle
stack against the installed package and mounts the theme. If it does not appear
after a restart, append `eva-inspired-theme` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the
profile's `package.json` — a package that is merely a dependency is not mounted.

## Remove

```
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove eva-inspired-theme
```

Drop the entry from `dsh.profile.bundles` too if you added it there.

## Layout

```
index.js              host half — mounts, registers no route, plays nothing
client.js             GENERATED browser bundle. Not tracked; build it. Do not edit.
src/client.js         service and effect orchestration
src/runtime/          private glass/pins/im/panels mounts
src/theme.css         the token layer
cordis.patch.yml      the bundle-patch mount declaration
build/                shipped assets + the two vendored client halves
build/wallpapers.json the TRACKED wallpaper manifest — art URLs, not image bytes
tools/                build, self-check, token audit
docs/                 design log, recon, audits, render reports, preview shots
NOTICE                upstream licences and third-party credits
LICENSE               this package's layered licence
LICENSE-CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.txt  the CC licence text for the brand marks
```

`client.js` is generated from `src/` and carries a banner saying so. Edit `src/`
and run `npm run build`; the check gate fails if the two drift apart.

The wallpaper manifest has two layers, and the tracked one names art instead of
carrying it:

- `build/wallpapers.json` — tracked. Two entries, each with a `direct:` URL that
  points at a third party's copy of the picture, plus the `page:` a credit
  belongs on. The build emits `url("https://…")`, so the theme keeps its
  background while this repository still holds no image bytes. An empty list is
  also legal: it publishes `--cp-pick-light: none; --cp-pick-dark: none;`, the
  paint layer's documented no-art state.
- `out/wallpapers.local.json` — ignored by git. The same shape with `dataUrl:`
  entries; if it exists the build reads it instead and embeds the art, which is
  how the maintainer's own machine keeps looking the way it does. `node
  tools/build-client.mjs --public` ignores it and builds the tracked form anyway.

Because `client.js` is ignored too, and the tracked manifest holds no `dataUrl:`,
a bundle that carries artwork has nowhere to be committed. Those facts are
asserted (`wall.2`, `wall.6`, `wall.7`, `wall.8`).

## Checks

```
npm run verify
```

Runs development gates: syntax checks, 25 behavioral/build-contract tests, 127
static assertions, the 55-token audit, and exact artifact/source comparison.
Build and check commands accept the same `--mode auto|public|local`; `--public`
remains an alias. A mismatched artifact/input fails rather than guessing by image format.

Release validation is `npm run verify:release -- --mode public --host-version
<exact-version>`. Fresh target-host evidence, collection time and input hashes
are required; old dumps without provenance yield a partial development audit,
not verified compatibility. `npm run measure:resources` measures local compression
and Node compilation, not browser performance. Build/prepare still default to
auto: release only from a clean isolated checkout without out/, then validate the
packed artifact's public mode. Shipped tools/*.mjs support source builds.

See [S1–S10 implementation and acceptance record](docs/optimization-s1-s10.md)
for limitations and rollback. No host profile was changed; the working artifact
was restored to local mode.

This package uses **tiered licensing**. Each licence applies only to the part it

Full terms: [LICENSE](LICENSE). Upstream texts and per-file credits:

# dsh-qqbot-muu > `@zaofan/dsh-qqbot` 的**扩展包 + 补丁集**：把社区插件补成一个能长期养的 QQ 助手 —— > 记得住人、分得清群、能自己写口播视频、有一个不会长歪的 2D 鲸鱼娘，还有一个主人说了算的 B 站运营流程。

界面截图含真实群名/昵称，默认不随仓库发布；需要市场截图时用本地脱敏版。

Node ≥ 22.5 · MIT · DSH 桌面端插件

--- ## 这是什么 一个**跑在你自己机器上**的 QQ 助手能力包。它不训练模型、不上传数据， 只是把「记忆、语气、出片、运营」这四件事用本地 SQLite + 本地小模型 + 云端算力拼成一条能跑的流水线： - **记忆**：两层记忆（个人层跨群统一 / 群层物理隔离）+ 类海马体的检索与巩固层 - **说话**：人格与世界书注入、本地小模型代答与单脑仲裁、TTS 发件箱、表情包准入 - **出片**：文案 → 分镜 → 出图质检 → 配音 → 字幕 → 拼片 → 草稿，主人一句「通过」才发 - **运营**：B 站扫码、单条分享卡片、AI 写评论草稿、审核后发送、数据留档 它**不是**：托管服务、SaaS、也不需要你的账号密码 —— 只有本机 Cookie 和本机数据库。 ## 功能 ### 记忆与认知 | 能力 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | 两层记忆 | 个人层（印象卡、熟识度）跨群统一；群层（台账、记忆、心情）按 scope 隔离，A 群的坏情绪不带坏 B 群 | | 统一记忆库 | 单个 `memory.db`（`node:sqlite` + WAL + FTS5），`chat` / `mem` 全部带 `scope` | | 类海马体检索 | 五路 RRF 融合：向量余弦 + 倒排关键词（二元组 + 单字）+ 实体锚定 + Pillow（只有文字动效 / 角色动效 / 出图质检需要；缺了会自动降级并如实记一条 warning） - ffmpeg（音效合成与拼片；找不到会静默降级为静音） ## 配置速查
装完要改的四个文件 - `dshqqbot/.qqbot-extensions/memory-config.json` → `dataRoot` 改成你的 bot 数据根（`install.mjs` 会自动替换标记位） - `dshqqbot/.qqbot-extensions/local-llm-config.json` → 同上 - `dshqqbot/.qqbot-extensions/draw-config.json` → 只有用本地 SD 绘图才需要改 - `dshqqbot/.qqbot-extensions/bili-ops-config.json` → B 站运营（`publish.mode` / 额度 / 定时）
群分级怎么配 浮窗「🧠 记忆」页 →「🏷 群等级」→ 设为关心 / 降为普通，即时生效。 同页「⭐ 特别关心」按**名字**加人/加群，界面上不会出现 openid： - 输入框填**群名**（如 `相亲相爱一家人`）或**昵称**（如 `木囿`）就能加，也接受直接粘 openid； - 下面「见过的群 / 说过话的人」候选点一下就是加/取消； - **聊天板块每条消息旁也有 ☆**，点一下就把这个人设为/取消特别关心 —— 不用再回来找名单； - 名单 chips 只显示名字，× 移除。 > 为什么不按群号 / QQ 号加？QQ 官方机器人接口只下发 `group_openid` / 用户 `openid`，**不给群号和 QQ 号**，本地也没有 号→openid 的映射表，所以按名字认人是最稳的一层。群名来自 `.qqbot/groups.json`，昵称来自消息台账（`msg-history`）。 名单里的**人**在普通群也会按关心级对待（完整召回 + 沉淀），写进 `priorityPeople`。也可以直接改 `data/group-tiers.json`： ```json { "defaultTier": "normal", "priority": ["群openid"], "priorityPeople": ["用户openid"], "normal": [], "profileInNormal": false, "digestNormal": false } ``` | 项 | 特别关心群 / 私聊 | 普通群（默认） | | --- | --- | --- | | 个人印象卡 | 完整卡 + 熟识度 | 只给一行「名字 · 等级」 | | 长期记忆召回 | 开 | 关 | | 长期记忆沉淀 | 开 | 关 | | 历史印象汇总 | 参与 | 不参与 | | 记忆分身读写 | 事实 + 个人卡 | 只记心情/关系，读最近 5 条 |
视频链路可调参数 | 项 | 默认 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `video.style` | `auto` | `auto` / `text`（文字动效 + 小蓝）/ `image`（真图分镜） | | `video.planner` | `true` | 分镜编排；`false` 退回「一屏一图 + 固定淡入」 | | `video.maxImageShots` | `2` | 一单最多几张真图（云端质量不可控，只花在开场和例证） | | `video.imageAttempts` | `3` | 每屏最多重画几次 | | `video.imageGate` | `true` | 出图质检开关（关掉 = 画完直接用） | | `video.imageGoodEnough` | `0.84` | 质检达标分，越高越挑 | | `video.character` | `true` | 文字屏是否带小蓝 | | `video.characterSize` | `300` | 小蓝落版尺寸（px） | | `video.shotMinSec` / `shotMaxSec` | `2.4` / `5.2` | 单屏时长上下限 |
B 站运营与工具调用 | action | 用途 | | --- | --- | | `plan topic=...` | 写脚本 → 出图 → 配音 → 字幕 → 拼片 → 封面 → 草稿（`awaiting_review`） | | `approve jobId=...` | 审核通过 → 自动投稿（失败退回成片包并给原因） | | `reject` / `publish mode=manual` / `comment` / `engage` / `rename` / `list` / `records` | 见浮窗与工具说明 | - `publish.requireApproval` 默认 `true`，`limits.dailyVideos` 默认 `1`，定时任务只产草稿、绝不自动发布。 - DeepSeek Key 不入库：优先读环境变量 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`，其次 `{dataRoot}/bili-ops-secret.json`（已忽略）。请求体只带选题/风格/分镜数/时长，不含聊天记录、记忆库、Cookie。 - 产物在 `{dataRoot}/.qqbot/bili-ops/jobs//`。 - 扩展工具用宿主**扁平 value-schema**：每个字段直接写 `{ type, description, enum?, required? }`，包成 JSON-Schema 的 `{ type:'object', properties }` 会被宿主拒绝，工具随即"消失"。
## 隐私 仓库内**不包含**任何真实 openid / 群号 / 聊天记录、B 站 Cookie、DeepSeek Key、 `memory.db`、运营产物、表情包图库与索引、模型缓存与日志。 `.gitignore` 是**白名单式**的（`*` 起手再 `!` 放行），只有源码、补丁、脚本、文档与截图能进仓库； `install.mjs` 也只复制代码与默认配置，不复制 `data/`、`.state/`、`*.bak`。 导入历史聊天记录时，**脱敏发生在入库之前**（不是事后补救）：手机号保留前 3 后 4、身份证前 6 后 4、 邮箱只留首字符、银行卡只留后 4 位、裸数字串按 QQ 号打码（年份与小额金额不受影响）。 可以先用 `--dry-run` 看筛出来哪些句子，确认后再写库。 ```bash # 只看报告，不写库 node qqbot-mod/scripts/qq-import.mjs --file 聊天记录.txt --dry-run # 只导入和某个人的对话（QQ 号最准，不会和同昵称的人串号） node qqbot-mod/scripts/qq-import.mjs --file 全部消息.txt --peer 123456789 --self-uin 987654321 --dry-run # 完整归档：整段对话原样进聊天台账，再用本地模型重建这个人的历史印象卡 node qqbot-mod/scripts/qq-import.mjs --file 全部消息.txt --peer 123456789 --self-uin 987654321 --archive --digest ``` | 参数 | 作用 | |---|---| | `--peer QQ号\|昵称` | 从「导出全部消息记录」里只捞出这一段对话。纯数字只认 QQ 号（防重名串号），昵称按规范化匹配 | | `--self-uin` / `--self-name` | 认出"我"。不给的话只能靠发言人数量猜：文件里非 peer 只有 1 个发言人 → 当作一对一；多个 → 只留对方的话并提示补号 | | `--archive` | 把**完整对话原样**写进 `chat` 台账：不筛寒暄、不砍长消息（默认 2000 字，实时采集是 500）。记忆分身、历史印象、"那晚到底聊了什么"都靠这份 | | `--scope` | 显式指定归档到哪个会话。默认按 QQ 号落在 `c2c:qq:<号>`，和运行时 openid scope 分开，不半截合并 | | `--digest` | 归档后调本地模型重建这个人的高维印象卡（切片→汇总） | | `--min-score` | 只影响**进记忆库**的筛选门槛，不影响归档 | 导入会同时产出三种东西，粒度不同、互不替代： 1. `chat` 台账 —— 原话，可重放、可事后换模型重建记忆； 2. `person:` 记忆 —— 筛掉寒暄后的句子 + 一条 `impression`（TA 是什么人）； 3. `person:` 里的 `relation` —— 一条"我们怎么相处"：轮次、谁先开口、回得多快、共同话题。 只靠"TA 说了什么"看不出关系，这一条是双方视角。 > 归档进台账的 `src='import'` 行**不吃 60 天保留窗**。否则导进来的旧记录下次日维护就被当过期数据删掉。 ```bash node qqbot-mod/scripts/graph-enrich.mjs --scope person:qq12345 --dry-run # 看还有多少条待补图 node qqbot-mod/scripts/graph-enrich.mjs --scope person:qq12345 --limit 50 # 本地模型补三元组 ``` 补图只往图谱加边、不改正文，**全在本机跑**（`local-llm` 的 Ollama / OpenAI 兼容端点）， 聊天记录不出机器。模型没开时脚本会立刻退出并说明原因，不会空转。 彻底删除一个 scope 的全部记忆用 `purgeScope`（代码接口，含索引与画像）， 导出用 `exportScope`，两者都会在 `{dataRoot}/.qqbot/memory/_audit.jsonl` 留痕。 ### 为什么导不进 `.bak`？—— 密钥根本拿不到 QQ NT 的聊天库是 `nt_msg.db`（外加若干同族库），**SQLCipher 加密**。密钥不是写死在文件里的常量： 它在 QQ 登录时由服务端下发，只存在 QQ 进程内存里，而且随版本/账号变化。要"拿到密钥"等于去 dump 运行中的 QQ 进程内存再逆出派生逻辑 —— 这既不稳定（一升级就废），也不该由本插件做。所以本插件**不解密 `.bak` / `nt_msg.db`，也没有任何"密钥获取"功能**：这不是没做完，是这个方向本身不通。 能走通的只有官方导出这条路： 1. PC 版 QQ → 左下角 **≡ / 设置** → **消息管理器**（老版本在「工具 → 消息管理器」）； 2. 左侧选中群或好友，等它把历史同步下来（首次打开会转一会儿）； 3. 右上角 **导出消息记录** → 选 **`.txt`**（推荐，纯文本最稳）或 `.mht`； 4. 浮窗 → **记忆** → 「📥 导入历史」，把导出文件的**绝对路径**填进去（带空格要加引号）。 > 找不到"导出消息记录"？多半是这个会话还没落到本地库 —— 在消息管理器里点开它、往下翻到底， > 再试；仍没有就是精简版/渠道版 QQ，换官方 PC 版 NT 再导。手机端可以先「聊天记录迁移」到电脑。 `--file` 除了 `.txt` / `.mht`，也吃任意 `.json`；面板里的 `--peer` 输入框用来只捞某一段对话。 ### 本地语音（GPT-SoVITS / Breeze TTS 2 / IndexTTS-2.5） 默认走 edge-tts（在线、零本机占用、音色稳定，但音色是"播音腔"）。想换成自己训练的模型或 本地推理，改用 `provider:"http"`——插件只认 OpenAI 形状的 `POST /v1/audio/speech`， `skills/local-tts/adapter/server.py` 就是那层适配（**纯标准库，零第三方依赖**），把 GPT-SoVITS 的参数式 `/tts`、Breeze 的多部分上传、IndexTTS 的 `/tts` 全部翻译成同一个接口， 并保证吐出**真 mp3**。 **先看这张表再选**（浮窗「设置」页的引擎表就是它的实时版：端口亮不亮、模型多大、现在选的是哪套）： | 引擎 | 端口 | 本机模型占用 | 速度 | 适合 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `edge`（默认） | 无（云端） | 0 GB | 秒级 | 日常聊天，缺点是播音腔 | | `gsv` GPT-SoVITS | 9880/9881 | 1.75 GB | 接近实时 | **聊天即时语音首选**，5 秒参考音克隆 | | `breeze` Breeze TTS 2 q8 | 7860/9881 | 9.15 GB | ≈0.10× 实时（820ms/帧） | 生成一段展示音频，不适合对话 | | `index` IndexTTS-2.5 | 9890/9881 | 14.6 GB | RTF≈22–30（3.8s 音频要 88s） | **离线视频配音 / 读评论**，情感最自然；6GB 卡常驻 5.9GB | 分工建议：聊天走 `gsv`，视频配音走 `index`（`narrate_footage.py --voice xiaolan_emo` 已直通）。 ```bash # 1) 起服务（显存 6GB 只能二选一，默认 breeze） powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File skills\local-tts\scripts\start-services.ps1 -Backend breeze powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File skills\local-tts\scripts\start-services.ps1 -Backend gsv # 停止：同一个脚本加 -Stop # 2) 换引擎有两条路 # a. 浮窗「设置」页 → 引擎表 → 点「用这个方案」（走 POST /api/qqbot-settings/tts-engines，直接改 voice-config.json） # b. 手改 dshqqbot\.qqbot-extensions\voice-config.json（改一次就行） # "provider": "http", # "endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:9881/v1/audio/speech", # "model": "gsv", ← gsv / breeze / index # "voice": "xiaolan" ← gsv: xiaolan|gentle；breeze: breeze|breeze_design；index: xiaolan_emo|xiaolan_emo_soft ``` 几个必须知道的点： - **Breeze 也吃 OpenAI JSON**：`POST /v1/audio/speech` + `response_format:"mp3"` 会直接回 64kbps / 24kHz 的真 mp3（裸 24k s16le PCM 只出现在 multipart 路径）。它缺的是**克隆音色注册**—— 想用自己的参考音得先 `POST /v1/voices`（ref_audio + ref_text + name），之后用 `voice:""`。 适配层把这两步都做了，所以插件侧还是填一个 `endpoint` 就够。 - **Breeze 慢**：q8_0 在 3060 上约 **0.10× 实时**（≈820ms/帧，瓶颈是 depth decoder 的 15 次串行小 matmul）， 适合"生成一段展示音频"，不适合聊天随口回。日常对话用 GPT-SoVITS 或先留 edge。 - 探活口径：Breeze 是 `GET /health`（`/v1/model` 是 404），GPT-SoVITS 是 `/tts`； 适配层的 `/health` 会分别探这些上游，`reachable:false` 只代表上游没起，不代表适配层坏了。 - 合成失败会往 `.qqbot/tts/failures.log` 记一行（含 bytes / exit code / 原因）， 0 字节不再"悄悄删掉"。 - `voiceProfiles` 里的 `size` 写的是**在线合成、本地无模型**——别把它当成"模型 0MB"。 - **9881 不用手动起**：插件每次合成前先探端口，没开就自己 detached 拉起 `adapter/server.py --manage`（空闲 3 分钟回收显存）。群里再也不会出现「tts-http: fetch failed」。 - **显存被聊天模型占着怎么办**：6GB 卡上 `qwen2.5:7b` 常驻能吃掉 4.2GB，GSV 要 3.4GB 就起不来。 插件遇到「显存不够」会先让 Ollama 把模型吐出来（`keep_alive:0`，下次聊天它自己会重载，几秒）， 再重试一次；要是还腾不出来（浏览器 + QQ + 桌面端能占掉 3GB 多），就**临时回退 edge 在线语音**把这句话说出来， 并在 `failures.log` 记 `local-vram-short → 已回退在线语音`。人在群里听到的是声音，不是报错。 - **工具/语音报错不进群**：失败的原文只写 `.qqbot/tool-errors.jsonl`，群里由她自己用一句人话圆过去。 想恢复"把报错直接发到群里"的旧行为，设环境变量 `QQBOT_TOOL_ERRORS_ON_QQ=1`。 ### 本地模型什么时候在显存里？ 默认策略是**平时不在**：聊天回复、向量化（`nomic-embed-text` 那个 274MB）都带 `keep_alive:0`， 生成完就离开显存；看门狗每 20s 看一眼，没 pin 且闲置超过 60s 就把 Ollama 里的模型整体卸载。 需要用的时候再冷启（`qwen2.5:7b` 约 5~6s，`qwen2.5:1.5b` 约 2s）。 要「借住」一段时间的场景用 pin： | 场景 | 谁 pin | 有效期 | 到点后 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 小游戏（海龟汤 / 故事接龙 / 你问我答） | `game-lib` 开局 `pin('game')`，每步续期 | 12 分钟 | 收摊或超时 → `unpin` + 立刻卸载 | | 视频配音 / 长文本读评论 | 由脚本自己 pin | 调用方决定 | 同上 | 配置在 `dshqqbot/.qqbot-extensions/local-llm-config.json`： ```jsonc { "model": "qwen2.5:7b", "gameModel": "", // 给游戏单独指定模型；留空=跟 model 同一个 "keepAlive": "0", // 单次请求的 keep_alive，0 = 用完就走 "residency": { "enabled": true, "idleUnloadSec": 60, // 没 pin 又闲置多久就整体卸载 "pinnedKeepAlive": "10m", // 有 pin 期间单次请求的 keep_alive "looseKeepAlive": "0", "watchMs": 20000 // 看门狗间隔 } } ``` 想让游戏又快又不太笨：`"gameModel": "qwen2.5:1.5b"`（986MB，冷启 2s，出题偶尔跑偏但有本地题库兜底）； 想让它更会聊：留空走 `qwen2.5:7b`。显存只有 6GB 时别同时让别的程序占着。 ### 库体检与维护 记忆库有几种"不报错、只悄悄变差"的坏法：索引表没建上（关键词/实体/图谱三路召回全哑， 只剩向量）、WAL 没检查点（备份可能是残的）、prune 删了行但文件不缩小、一直没备份。 一个脚本全查一遍： ```bash node qqbot-mod/scripts/mem-maintain.mjs --data-root <数据目录> # 只体检，只读 node qqbot-mod/scripts/mem-maintain.mjs --data-root <数据目录> --fix # 检查点 + 备份 + 补索引 node qqbot-mod/scripts/mem-maintain.mjs --data-root <数据目录> --fix --vacuum --keep 5 ``` 体检会明确回答「倒排覆盖 487/489」「缺表: mem_edge」「碎片率 34%」这类问题， 而不是给一个"正常"。日常备份不用手动：`chatlog.dailyBackup` 会在每日维护窗口 把库 `VACUUM INTO` 到 `.qqbot/backups/`，保留 `backupKeep` 份。 ## 目录 ```text dshqqbot/.qqbot-extensions/ 扩展本体（inbound / outbound / hooks / tools / lib） qqbot-mod/patches/ 客户端与服务端补丁（--check / --apply / --revert） qqbot-mod/patches/live-overlay/ 官方原文件 + 定制版 + 三路合并安装器（扛插件自动升级） qqbot-mod/scripts/ 自检脚本（`node qqbot-mod/scripts/run-all-tests.mjs` 一把跑完 51 个套件，失败详情落 tmp/test-failures/） qqbot-mod/persona/ 人格与世界书（唯一事实源） assets/char/pose/ 鲸鱼娘五姿态（720×980 透明 PNG + sprite.json，video.character 直接用） assets/char/src/ 出图原图（带底色，供重抠/换姿态） assets/char/whale/ 同配色纯鲸鱼本体（贴纸/小图标用） skills/video-frame-render/ 逐帧拼视频的 skill（Pillow 画帧 + ffmpeg 编码，省 token） skills/local-tts/ 本地 TTS 适配层（OpenAI 形状 /v1/audio/speech → GPT-SoVITS / Breeze / IndexTTS） skills/voice-sing/ 唱歌换声（Demucs 拆轨 → RVC 换声 → 混音；带 sources.json 出处台账） docs/publish-flow.md 第一条视频从选题到投稿的完整流程（首跑记录，含踩过的坑与验收口径） assets/ README 截图与图标 submission/ 插件市场提交条目 install.mjs 把扩展装进任意 bot 数据根 ``` ## 市场收录 - 条目：`submission/wuwo1979__dsh-qqbot-muu.yml`（`category: usage`） - 截图：`screenshots.json`（仓库根，相对路径，最多 8 张） - 本地预检：`node scripts/check-submission.mjs` —— 校验 YAML 字段、`dsh.bundle` 声明、图标与截图规则，提交前先跑一遍就不会再被 CI 打回来 ## 致谢与许可 - 基础插件：`@zaofan/dsh-qqbot`（客户端 `client/qqbot-settings.js`、`dist/features/*`） - 本项目在其之上补扩展与补丁，与插件作者无隶属关系 - MIT
